title: Product appears to be excellent, packaging not so much
text:
About 30 years ago, I cracked a tooth. The dentist told me it was from bruxism and said I needed to get a night guard. I got one of the standard wraparound type. A year or two later, I cracked another tooth. I had also chewed through a couple of night guards. This went on for several years with me cracking a tooth every 2-3 years, many resulting in root canals.

Finally, I did some research and found the NTI, a small bite guard that fits over the front teeth. The theory was that the wrap-around night guards actually made the bruxism worse because they sit between the morals, which are the brushing and teeth grinding. When they feels pressure, they tend to clamp down. This made some sense to me since I was chewing through the wraparound night guards.

The NTI had to be custom made by a dentist because, being small, they were a choking risk, so had to fit snugly over the teeth so they could not easily become loose and be aspirated. The going rate around here was about $500-$600 dollars. I decided to give it a try, because it was cheaper than crown and root canals.

I got my NTI about 20 years ago and have not had a cracked tooth since. However. about 7-8 years ago, the softer interior material started to wear and crack. The NTI no longer fit tightly against my teeth. I wasn’t too worried about aspiration because I never sleep on my back. But over the past year or two, almost all of the interior material has fallen out. The NTI is now so loose that it sometimes digs into the inside of my lip.

Before I spent about $600 for a new NTI, I did a little checking and discovered the Smart Guard. It looked like it might be the same job as the4 NTI and it cost a fraction of the cost. So I ordered one. It arrived today. I just completed the fitting procedure, so here’s my initial review. I’ll try to update it in a few weeks after I have used it for awhile.

The fitting instructions were pretty easy and I was able to complete them without a problem. It seems to fit fairly tightly – not as tight as the NTI, but I don’t think it will slip off. And it’s quite a bit larger than the NTI so much harder to aspirate. I give it an A- or B+ for instructions and fitting.

Here’s the bad news. This version, which is supposed to be “improved”, does not come with a case. This is a major problem, especially since I understand that previous version came with a case and two guards. This will cost it at least one full star. What am I supposed to do, just leave it out on the night stand? And what do I do when I travel, just toss it in the suitcase with the underwear?

Worse, the instructions say to keep the night guard in its “storage case”. I guess they just used the same instructions as for the previous version which did have a case. Deduct half a star.

The instructions are pretty good, but who keep paper instructions anymore? The folded instruction sheet is the wrong size for scanning and there is no downloadable PDF version on their website. Deduct another half star.

This is really too bad. With a little better follow through, this could have been a 5-star product. They appear to have done the hard part right. Pity.

title: They do work mostly
text:
Since I've started using these my dental hygienist has raved about the condition of my gums. So I'm going to say the technology works. Unfortunately the execution of this particular device leaves something to be desired.

I can't comment on these devices crapping out after one or two uses, but I have found that not all apparently dead ones are in fact done for. I've found that some will come back to life if they're charged correctly.

The little metal pieces must be lined up just so and stay that way during the entire charge cycle. Unfortunately it's very easy to misalign the parts or to jostle them out of alignment. A pair of magnifying eyeglasses and a very steady charging station are invaluable here.

Although this has been a (temporary?) solution for me, this company is crazy to sell a consumer item whose maintenance is so exacting. They could at least warn people to take care when setting up the device for recharge.

Please note that Starlight Smile also sells a corded device. I haven't used one so can't comment, but if recharging this one continues to be a nightmare, I'll probably try it. My gums and my hygienist are happy, and it's worth some trouble to keep that going.

title: An improvement to the more common "Y" type flossers.
text:
This review is for the N Noble One Oral Picks Replaceable Self-Cut Dental Floss Holder. I have ginormous hands and hate trying to use my fingers to reach into my mouth to floss. I had hoped this design would be an improvement over my GUM Flossmate, and it was!

PROS:
-Floss is stored and fed from the handle.
-Design allows you to continuously feed a small amount of 'clean' floss to the head, and remove excess off the end with a built in cutter so wastage is minimal.
-Small head easily fits into mouth and is easily maneuvered around while flossing.
-Floss track works and keeps the floss were it needs to be - I have not seen the floss slip out like I did on the "Y" style flossers.

CONS:
-The design utilizes a small blue plastic cap between the handle and the nub (see the photo) in an attempt to friction lock the floss in place and keep it from feeding slack when in use. It doesn't work, but there is a work around - see below.

Initially I found that I could can only floss one or two teeth before cap allowed enough slack to occur that I could not continue flossing. Fortunately, there is an easy work around. Ditch the blue cap and just use the nub to lock down the floss in both directions. It's a little bit of a pain to unwind it (twice), but it works and I was already doing that with my Flossmate so it was nothing new to my routine.

We have never used the prior version Kandoo sensative flushable wipes so we can't compare the new version with the old. I do believe the reason for making them smaller/thinner is so it will not clog your toilet..I am guessing maybe the previous version did so they had to make this change. Makes sense to me.

We still need these wipes for him since his bottom is so very sensative & like the idea of flushing them after use. So how we work around the issues of these wipes is by getting a wad of toiler paper if you will then putting 1 sheet of the flushable wipe on top of it so it helps with a messy clean up without tearing or having to use the entire pack. We do this each time as we are wiping his bottom (get wad of toilet paper with 1 sheet of flushable wipe on top). This has worked extremely well for us! We love the idea of no longer having to carry around sensative throw away wipes & disposable diaper throw away bags to contain the odor. And we do not have to go through a lot of the actual flushable wipes since we use it along with a wad of toilet paper.

Hope this helps!

title: Don't overlook Amazon's Solimo
text:
Chapped, dry, and bleeding hands are no joke and I have probably experienced the worst it can get while working in a machine shop (prior to CNC) and doing assorted mechanic work out in my garage. When really dry, it felt like my hands were going to fall off at the wrists, and I'll always remember the excruciating pain.

It was some time around the 1960's that specialty hand soaps for mechanics began appearing in the car parts stores. They were a bit of a miracle to watch as the gel just effortlessly lifted all that grease off the hands. But this new miracle solution worked so well it would also dry out the hands until years later when somebody thought to include lanolin in the mix. That finally changed everything for mechanics who no longer had to show up at the dinner table with grease still embedded in their dry, chapped, and bleeding hands.

Up until then there was LAVA soap (still in production today) but that's like scrubbing your hands with a brick. The highly abrasive mixture would sting and didn't work well on dry chapped hands, doing nothing to help heal them or diminish the pain involved. There were some special lotions like Corn Huskers and Vaseline Jelly (probably the oldest) for repairing dry, sick skin, but it would be used up too quickly and it might take weeks before remembering to buy more.

Now that I'm retired I haven't had dry skin or bleeding fingers for the past ten years, but it doesn't mean the hands still won't chap when neglected. Vaseline Medicated Intensive Care lotion was my favorite up until they took it out of production, nearly putting me into a panic. Vaseline introduced a replacement that worked even better, called Vaseline Deep Moisturizing lotion with 30% Petrolatum and had the same consistency as tooth paste. A little dab will do ya' on the back of the hands on a daily basis. But I quit buying it recently because Vaseline now contracts it out to other cosmetic companies, and the price is soaring to about $10 for 4.5 ounces while the quality continues to go south. So now I'm using Amazon's Solimo, likely made using Vaseline's own 100% White Petrolatum Jelly that has proven for a couple of centuries now to be better and Amazon has it priced lower than everything else.

There really is no need for anyone to suffer from dry, rough skin with the hundreds of lotions and treated soaps that are now available, all intended to remove that greasy feeling that women make very obvious how much they despise. Typically, most men couldn't care less how it feels provided it does what it claims. The best ones all seem to contain at least one ingredient of either lanolin, or petrolatum, or glycerin, and even menthol. There is a whole flock of ingredients listed in other products that have such long complicated names they can't even be pronounced. Oddly enough, those are the same ones that cost the most, whereas my little 7.5 ounce jar of Solimo that cost three bucks only contains just one ingredient: 100% White Petrolatum Jelly. A little dab on the back of the hand soaks into the skin quickly and the jar will last a couple of years positively keeping my hands absolutely free of dry, chapped, and bleeding fingers. And for that, I am very thankful. So there you go.

title: Prep Refresher = Brilliant Complexion
text:
I am a Black woman in my late 30s who has been dealing with cystic acne for the better part of 10 years. Over the last year especially I have been dealing with the scarring from this acne and have been experimenting with tons of products that can both deal with the cystic acne and the scarring with little success. But I have found that only glycolic acid works and after reading the reviews for this toner I thought that it couldn't hurt to try. I wanted to wait to see what it would do for my skin before writing a review and the results have been nothing short of remarkable. It's been about 5 days since I received it and started using: It has lessened the darkening of some of the scars and a few of the lighter ones are so faint I can't remember how dark they were before using. My pores were larger and my skin used to be oily to the point of embarrassment and now my complexion is much smoother, clearer and more matte. I took pictures of my skin before I began using and when I looked back at them (before writing this review to make sure it wasn't just my imagination) I can easily see a huge, huge difference!

I use it morning and night. I also received a free small bottle of collagen facial wash by Cellbone that was included in my order and it too is awesome. I wash with that, use a cotton pad (vs. a cotton ball, the pads for me are easier) to apply the Prep Refresher on my face and neck, and allow it to work -- I feel a tingling sensation that's mostly bearable (!) and when it subsides I apply aloe vera gel over my whole face, let that dry which it quickly does, then a moisturizer with SPF on top of it. I am so happy with this product and may go for a professional glycolic peel in a month if the deeper, darker scars are still apparent. I always get nervous too because with my Black skin I don't want to use a product that will cause more hyperpigmentation. I am going to call Cellbone to see if or when I should take a break from using this product or if it's safe enough to use everyday for an extended period of time. But overall I am completely happy with this product.

(Shipping from Cellbone was almost $7, high by my standards)

title: Finally getting my self-esteem back!!
text:
First of all, everyone understands how one's facial appearance is directly tied to one's self-esteem. For me, my self-esteem is directly tied to Cellbone's Prep Skin Refresher!!!! I won't ever stop using this product.

A little about me/my skin: I am a 42-yr old Asian-Pacific Islander and have medium-tone skin, which essentially translates into severe post-acne hyperpigmentation anytime I break out. I never broke out as a teenager so it was so strange to me that I started breaking out badly the last 2 years. (I attribute most of it to job-stress so I really figured there was nothing I could do about my poor complexion). I recently saw a photo of myself from 2009 where I had no makeup on, and I pratically cried. I had forgotten that I had GREAT skin up until recently. I had gotten into this vicious cycle as of late: wearing concealer & makeup to hide the dark hyperpigmentation, which I'm certain resulted in more breakouts = more hyperpigmentation. It was just awful!! I was at my wit's end. I couldn't get my skin under control even with prescription drugs.

In January, I began both salycylic & glycolic acid treatments, and those helped the hyperpigmentation somewhat. I continued to breakout a bit and was willing to suffer through the breakouts in hopes that things were merely getting worse before they would get better. In March, I took a nearly 3-week long trip to hot, dusty Tanzania (climbed Mount Kilimanjaro, went on safari, & then chilled out on Zanzibar). Well, I was without the comforts of home for the majority of that trip so I used pre-moistened face wipes & hot water (when it was available) to cleanse my face & always followed up with the Prep Skin Refresher. Translation: I was hot,sweaty, & dusty/dirty the majority of the time. My breakouts stopped "dead in their tracks," and my hyperpigmentation appeared to improve. Upon my return from my trip, I continued with the Prep Skin Refresher post-face wash and have only had 2 glycolic treatments since I returned.

I can't believe how my complexion is improving!! I'm actually not scared to look in the mirror now, and I'm no longer morbidly depressed about how I look without makeup. I know it's definitely this Cellbone product that has attributed to my vast improvement. (While the glycolic acid treatment does help, I'm only doing that every other week). I'm using the Prep Skin Refresher daily, usually in the a.m. & in the p.m. I haven't changed any other face, body, or hair products--so I know it wasn't an allergy. Again, I was using this product religiously when I was camping on Mount Kilimanjaro (hey, I didn't shower for 6 nights, but I still didn't break out!!!!)

I also have before & "so far" pictures, so I have an objective gauge as to my improvement. I would like my skin to get a bit better before I'm brave enough to post the pictures for you all, but stay tuned. I'll update this review when I get up enough nerve to add the pictures. I don't know what's in this stuff, but I SWEAR it's worth trying if you have acne/hyperpigmentation. I've been using this since the beginning of March, and I still have half the bottle left.

I hope others who are "suffering in silence" will give this a shot. I think it's a small price to pay to help your self-esteem! Also, Cellbone threw in 2 other free samples that I haven't tried yet (I didn't want to "waste" the product on my poor skin, but I'll try them this weekend). Cellbone: you have a customer for life. Please please please don't get rid of this Prep!!!

title: SAVED MY SKIN! Updated review. 18 months of use now. No more acne
text:
Updated review 8.30.2013. I have been using this product for about 18 months. Still very happy with the product after using it a year. I have multiple repeat purchases of the product and it is still working well to keep my skin smooth and clearer than it would otherwise be without using this product.

I am 37 years old and I have been fighting a pitched battle with my acne prone skin since my earliest teens. Acne is a complex problem with a lot of causes.
I have used this product for about nine months. My skin absolutely looks amazing now. It GLOWS. I can actually leave the house WITHOUT MAKEUP and not feel ashamed anymore.
By glow, I mean it looks darn near flawless. I am getting compliments on my skin for the first time in my life.

I have sensitive skin. A word of caution:
Prep Skin Refresher CAN and DOES sting until your skin becomes accustomed to it. Work through it because the results are WORTH EVERY MINUTE of slight (or not so slight) discomfort.
The first time I used it I thought I couldn't handle it. I washed it off with water after about five minutes. I was mad at first but my skin was so smooth! The glow on my skin was unmistakeable and my makeup went on so smoothly I was astounded.

I decided to try again the next day. I repeated the process. wipe on, let sit for five minutes, rinse off. I had to do this for a few weeks until my sensitivity subsided.
I can now put on the product and it does not sting at all.

I use this product on my entire face, neck, chest, and upper arms. I follow with a good clean moisturizer.
In the summer, I use it on my legs to make them smoother. It does sting after you shave or exfoliate so plan accordingly.
I shave or exfoliate at least 10 to 12 hours BEFORE or AFTER using this product.

My other secret weapon is a Glycolic acid pumpkin mask. i use these two products together for smooth glowing skin.

title: Read Here For Our Regimen (This Product Is An Integral Part)
text:

I'm a 30-something mom who also has acne from time to time, resulting in temporary acne scarring.

This stuff is great. Here's what we've been doing:

Once per week, we each do a Lactic Acid 70% peel for a minute or two.

Each night (except the Lactic Acid night) we cleanse and then swipe with this skin prep toner.

Then we use the 100% pure Hyaluronic acid, once that soaks in we top it with a few drops of 100% pure Moroccan Argan oil.

If you like to have bits of flowers and plants floating in the water as you bathe, ignore the rest of this paragraph. If, like me, you’d prefer to avoid picking bits of lavender blossoms off of your tub after bating, throw the bomb into a mesh bag or pantyhose stocking before putting it in the water. title: Zinc Oxide has a lot of uses, but is in LOTS of products.
text:
How amazing is it that one can make their own sunscreen, deodorant, diaper rash cream, etc and know exactly what is in it and make it the way you want it! Make it scented or unscented by adding essential oils.

This does NOT come with instructions on making your own products, but it's easy enough to do Internet searches to find recipes to make your own products. You can control what SPF is in your products by following recipes found online. You can use it on skin wounds and it aids in healing. I know when I worked as a nurse, I would see Zinc oxide as an ingredient in creams/ointments and unna boot wraps. There is Zinc oxide in many more products than most realize.

In researching the benefits and uses of Zinc oxide powder, I learned Zinc oxide can be used on energy saving and as a heat protectant on windows! Hello lower electric bill in the summer! Applying a coating to Windows helps keep heat inside rooms, let's visible light in and reflects infrared radiation.

Can be used as a skin astringent. Zinc can act as a skin drying agent, help relieve inflammation/irritation/reduce rashes. Likewise, it can be used for dandruff, dry/itchy scalp (intact is in many commercial brands of anti-dandrruff products). Likewise, Zinc is in many kinds of make up also. It just has a wide array of uses!

With all that being said, and I know I'm leaving a LOT of other things that could be mentioned, I am over all satisfied with this Zinc oxide bulk package from Plant Guru, but would be nice to include some instructions, as not everyone will know to research how to use this.

☆☆DISCLAIMER: I did receive this Plant Guru Zinc Oxide powder at a discounted price in exchange for my own honest, unbiased, and own original opinion. However, my rating ONLY reflects my opinion of the powder. Not the price.

title: Many Uses for Zinc Oxide.
text:
I love this zinc oxide powder! You can look up recipes using zinc oxide powder and find many uses with instructions, including sun screen, diaper rash cream, lip balm, deodorant, and probably much more. In addition to the "recopies" you can also add this in to lotion you already have. It is such a fine powder that it mixes in extremely well. I do suggest wearing a paint or medical mask since it can get into the air if you're breathing over it as you get the powder out of the bag.
A great attribute of this particular zinc oxide powder is the sturdy resealable bag it comes in. You would have to try really hard to puncture the bag. Because it's tough, you could throw it in a suitcase without worrying about it getting everywhere. Once we get to our vacation destination, we'll mix up several containers of sunscreen. You can actually mix this in a bowl and seal it or put it into plastic bottles.
Since Tommy and our youngest son do a lot of surfing everyday, a heavy mix of zinc oxide lotion to coat onto their nose and under eyes is a must. The lotion sits at the top of the skin to protect those points on their faces that often get sunburned. It does not soak in. Keep in mind that this also means they have white face paint but so do a ton of other surfers so that's normal in our surroundings.
This is the first time I've done DIY sunscreen and If i had know this years ago I would have saved a fortune. We all know what the prices are like, I try to get it when it's on sale but it still does sting the wallet a bit. I received a free bag of zinc oxide powder and in return agreed to try it out and leave my honest opinion in this review. It's definitely a very handy item to have around! Do a search to find suggestions on how to make an assortment of zinc oxide items.

The reading portion of the lenses is a little too small to let me see an entire page at once, but I quickly adapted to slightly lifting and lowering my head as needed while reading. Another plus is being able to read my cell phone screen without having to remove my sunglasses and put on readers. I was concerned that the bifocals might look dorky, but you can barely tell they are there when looking straight on.

When I first put them on, the side pieces pressed firmly against the side of my head. At first I thought they were too tight, but I left them on and within a couple of minutes did not notice any discomfort. The snug fit keeps them seated on my face and they don't slip down my nose even with sweat and suntan lotion. After successful use at the beast, I've made them my go-to pair for daily use.

title: Very glad I purchased these
text:
I only received these a few days ago, so I can say nothing about durability yet -- if that changes in a negative way, I'll update this review. But they certainly feel durable. I've been using OTC saline sprays (aka Ocean) for decades due to sinus issues (including narrow sinus passageways that clog too easily). But recently, I started reading about one of the ingredients in those sprays -- it's more than just salt and water -- and didn't like what I read; I'd experienced the symptoms reported due to that ingredient: initially good, but then membranes dry out uncomfortably. Since I've used homemade saline solutions for years to flush my sinuses with a bulb, I tried emptying an OTC bottle then refilling it with my own saline solution. It worked OK, but as always, the dose is more of a squirt than a spray.

So, I tried these. SO glad I did. They produce a very fine spray that's very comfortable. Two or three 'squirts" per nostril, blow my nose, one more per nostril and I'm good for hours. I've filled both with my saline solution, and one will remain home while the other rides in my everyday pack.

In the end I had to use the analog (red & white) leads and hook them up to the cable box - which means that only programming that originates with cable TV is delivered through the device. Well, I'd like it to feed all the sound which relates to the TV, but none of the analog ports from the TV produced sound in these earbuds. So, for example, when I'm streaming something and the sound does come from the TV it still doesn't feed this device. Believe me, I tried all the plugs. If anyone can tell me why this is and what to do about it I would greatly appreciate the guidance. Furthermore, the extra functions that this hearing enhancer offers are pretty much not on my list of needs - but there they are and I have to pay for them too. Why doesn't this company make a device that is specifically for TV sound, and then explain that it is not going to work except when hooked up to the cable box. Lastly, the earbuds that came with it are supposed to be mute-able, but that does not work. So I have to listen to the ads or take the buds out of my ears. Something very GOOD about this device is that I can walk away from the TV and around the corner and work in the kitchen and the sound from the TV comes with me. title: Crisp sound directly from electronic devices
text:
A streamer that shoots sound (music, movies, computer) wirelessly into your hearing aids gives much clearer sound. For a while I bulked at the high price of the Oticon ConnectLine TV 3.0 for Oticon Opn. But I jumped for it when it went on sale (from Hearing_Aid_Accessories in the UK), and I'm glad that I did. The sound is awesome.

You pair your hearing aids once to the streamer. Pairing adds a new mode; so now I have NORMAL, CLASSROOM, and STREAMER; hold down the right HA button for three seconds to move to the next mode. Five minutes with no sound moves you from STREAMER to back NORMAL mode, presumably to save battery power; sometimes this is convenient and sometimes not -- but it takes only a few seconds to bring STREAMER mode back. The connection is very stable; if the sound starts breaking up, change the batteries -- they are almost dying anyway. You can move a pretty good distance and still keep the connection; this is good for doing exercise videos or for jumping on a trampoline during football games.

The photo shows my setup. My external speakers are on the bottom; the top has a 4-output amplifier on the left and the Oticon streamer on the right, both secured to the top by velcro strips. The wired amplifier input goes into the back of my TCL TV and gives whatever sound goes with the main screen (computer, TV, Roku streaming, whaever). Amplifier output 1 goes into the speakers underneath, 2 and 3 go into pillow speakers (these give quite good sound when your head with HAs rest on the speaker -- this is a a cheaper alternative but limits mobility), and 4 goes to the Oticon streamer (with the amplifier at max -- click the hearing aids to regulate volume). While I can adjust the sound of all four independently, I use the streamer most of the time.

If you want the sound louder, max the volume on your hearing aids and lower the audio going into the streamer. If you overload the streamer, the audio quality suffers.

For additional HA and streamer features, get the free OTICON ON app for your android or apple phone.

If you're on the fence, buy this device -- the sound is amazingly good.

title: This works great!
text: I have a full growth pattern of hair but I still like a buzzed head. I went to a high end barber a few times and got a straight razor shave, but my hair returned so quickly my nice shiny bald head was gone in no time. I have so many little speed bumps on my scalp that I’d bleed profusely if shaved it myself with one of my Gillet face razor. Therefore I’ve been using my 00000 blade on my electric hair trimmer to get it as short as I can. It’s messy and a pain to clean up. THEN, an add for a competing brand of this razor showed up in my Instagram feed. I immediately went to my Amazon app and reviewed all of them. Reading mixed reviews about effectiveness and durability, I bought the cheapest one ($29.99) with the highest rating. I’ve only used it a few times so I can’t comment on durability. But, the first time I dry shaved. I didn’t want to test the “waterproof” claim but it worked well. The next time I jumped in the shower with it using plain water. It cut a bit closer. Tonight I thought I’d try it in the shower with my beard shaving soap and see if it got gooped up and didn’t work well. It worked fabulously. After a few laps around my head I’d simply hold it up to he shower head to blast it clean.  No matter the method, you do have to go back and forth and round and round to get your whole head nice and smooth. Other than that, this thing is fabulous. It rinses clean easily and charges quickly. I have a goatee without a mustache and it does a poor job of shaving my upper lip and nostril area so I just clean that up with my shave razor.  Anyhow, I am super pleased as this makes a previously nasty job to a painless and clean one.

text:

Cut to now.... I thought I'd give it another try. I decided to go with the variety pack this time and I'm SO GLAD I DID.

The two curved guys (think pear curved) work WONDERFULLY on your face.
I'll never go back to the old straight one and I don't understand what to do with the three-coiled dude with the squeezy handle. Nonetheless, I'm very happy with two of the items which was more than I hoped for.

I did see in the other reviews that someone said "doesn't work". I'm not sure if she/he tried all of them but now, when I use the straight model (which you curve and spin with your fingers), I really couldn't get it to work, which was odd since I've used them before. The pre-curved ones really do work well though.

So long, mustache.

title: Experience after 6 months
text:
This callus remover worked very well from the first day. It was powerful, easy to use, and very effective. After a little more than 5 months, the drive mechanism began to fail. The motor continued to run smoothly, but the connection between the motor and the roller began to slip. It made a loud, very unpleasant screeching sounds, and was basically unusable. The product came with a 1 year warranty, so I was somewhat optimistic.

When I contacted the manufacturer, Emjoi, they told me that the warranty was the responsibility of the company that sold me the product. At that point I realized that I did not buy this directly from Amazon but from a vendor called ShaveNow. A little research led me to an email address for Customer Service at ShaveNow. My inquiry was answered in a matter of hours. After providing copies of the relevant paperwork, I was given a mailing address for the return. I sent the unit in, and a couple of weeks later, they sent me a new Callus Remover. Not some refurb -- a full, brand new, retail package containing a new product.

I can't give 5 stars for a product that failed after 5 months of use, but overall, I'm still feeling good about the purchase. if I could, I would certainly give ShaveNow 5 stars for customer service.

title: Review and comparrison of this model to the Own Harmony
text:
I just received my Emjoi Micro-Pedi POWER - Callus Remover today and used it. Before I go any further, I need to mention that before getting this model, I had the Own Harmony unit. I loved the Own Harmony that I had.

It was easy to use, and easy to clean. The only reason that I sent it back and got this one is because the Own Harmony is no Electric, is spite of their claims. The Own Harmony is actually a rechargeable battery. Im guessing that they think they can get away with saying it is Electric because you use Electricity to recharge the batteries.

Because the Own Harmony runs on batteries, it is not very powerful. I found that the rollers stopped rolling a lot when I was using it. I also found each time I charged it, it because less and less powerful. So I returned it for a refund and got this one.

Ok, now on to the review of the Emjoi Micro-Pedi POWER - Callus Remover. If you did not try the Own Harmony 1st, you might not know or miss these features that I am going to be talking about. But since I did try the Own Harmony before I had this one, there are certain things that I did not like on this one.

Pros

I love, love, love that the Emjoi Micro-Pedi POWER - Callus Remover is actually Electric. This makes it pretty powerful. I have pretty tought calluses, so I need a powerful unit and this one seems to deliver.

The power cord is pretty long, so for me, I can plug it in and still sit in my shower to use. If you dont have a plug in close to your bath or shower, you might have to use an extension cord. I think there will be some that will fall into this category, so I deducted 1 star because their cord is not longer. So I listed the cord as both a pro and con since it will depend on how far away your outlet is.

Con
Power cord is not long enough. Some people will probably wind up having to use an extension cord.

Hard to clean
If you have not used another unit like the Own Harmony, you might not know what you are missing. But, since I did use the Own Harmony 1st, I have to note this as a Con on this unit The Own Harmony is a breeze to clean. The roller has no protective cover, so it more exposed that one this unit. On this unit, the protective cover clogs up with skin that is being removed. This unit also has areas on it that skin gets into that are hard to get out of even with water or the brush they provide. The Own Harmony wins on clean up hands down!!

Rollers
Maybe it was because I was used to the rollers on the Own Harmony, but I liked them much better than on this model. They do not seem as rough and look to be not as durable, but the durability I wont be able to attest to for a while since I just got it. Also the way you remove the rollers is not near as easy as the Own Harmony.

Protective Shied
According to the manual, this protective shied is what goes over the roller and I guess is supposed to protect you. But for me, this protecting cover for the roller just gets in the way. Let me explain. With the Own Harmony, almost the entire roller is exposed, so I can use the device on any area of my foot with no problem. With the Emjoi Micro-Pedi, there is certain areas of my foot that are curved, like around the arches, that are very hard to use the device on because of this protective cover. So again, the Own harmony wins hands down.

So in summary, for the Emjoi Micro-Pedi POWER I love love love that it is a true electric. But in every other category, the Own harmony is the winner. If only the Own harmony was electric instead of battery powered, it would be my hands down choice.

text:
Update after 18 months of use:

Still the best callus remover I have ever found. Absolutely 100% recommend. Before purchasing this I had nearly constant foot pain, and nothing I found could adequately deal with my calluses. Since I bought this, my problem has been solved.

The few negative reviews all site the same basic complaint: It is not powerful enough. That is due to the power supply that they chose to include. It has ample power at full speed, but the power drops off as you slow it down, and even slightly below full speed it becomes unusable. To me that is not an issue. I prefer it at full speed anyway, but for others it might be an issue.

They claim the new version addresses the problem. I don't know if that is true or not, but I would still not hesitate to recommend this.

--- Original Review ---
By far the best callous remover I have found. Mechanically, it is very simple and should be reliable. The consumables are dirt cheap and easy to use. And it just works. My feet are in better shape than they have been in in years.

The not quite perfect:

* Having the power switch and speed control on the cord is annoying. It works, but it is a pain to use. Personally,.I only use it at full speed, so it is not a huge deal. The bigger issue is that if the wall wart fails, you just replace it with a standard power supply. Integrating the speed controller into the device would make it far more reliable.
* For most parts of my foot, the design is great, but it would be nice if it had a sort of pistol grip handle to reach the callouses on the bottom of my foot.

Neither of these issues are deal breakers. I've tried the Emjoi and similar callous removers and different manual tools, but this works far better.

text: Firts, this is a good product.  I don't want to say they are a poor product, but I want to caution people depending on their needs.  My masks were not being held tight enough to my face, so I got these to hopefully tighten them.  They work as advertised in terms of how they function, and I'm sure that there are a lot of people who it would work for.  The mechanism for attaching them to the ear loops is much better than I thought.  The little "button" that slides into the loop is attached to fabric, not a rigid material.  The result is that there is no problem attaching them to most any thickness of ear loop material.  However,for me, it was too long.  I adapted them to work by looping it around on ear loop and attaching it to the other ear loop, essentially cutting it in half.  It is adjustable, but the shortest length is still 5 1/2 inches long, which I may have missed in the description.  That is way too long for my purposes.  I think part of the reason is that my ear loops are elastic, and when stretched far enough, the distance between them is much shorter.  My advice, measure the distance between the loops when you pull them back far enough for you.  Elastic loops may give more than you think.

Being a guy I hate having my pockets filled with a lot of stuff so I ordered this in hopes I could keep them on my belt. It works great. Since I need to carry two pens this worked great. Both fit in it nice and it clips to the belt nice and it does not look to big and bulky. I need to dress up everyday for work and it looks nice, I ordered black with blue decal.

title: Very durable case
text: This product goes through some serious abuse from my day to day activities. I install hurricane shutters. I go camping, hiking and geocaching every chance I get. This case has been through it all with me. It's nice looking and not to bulky if you need to attach it to your belt or pants. Just watch that you pull the velcro patch down all the way to keep your epipen inside.

title: I've Owned at Least Three and Will Be Ordering a Fourth
text:
I've owned at least three of these Epipen holsters. They're well-made, secure, and the synthetic cloth looks like new even two years on. I think they look good, too. Very functional. I recommend getting a good matching carabiner to more securely hook it to your belt. The holster has a loop at the top designed for this.

Far better than the branded Epipen holsters I used to have. Those things looked bad after six months.

However, after about two years, I've found the clip snaps off. It's still functional with the carabiner, but it doesn't ride as high and tends to bounce around. Prior to the clip snapping off, the faux leather material they use around the clip wears off. Again, still functional, but it might be a little rough on your dress pants if you wear it a lot.

I'm about to order another because of the clip issue. If they could fix that problem, this would be the ideal solution and would deserve five stars.

Also... sometimes people mistake it for a multitool, knife, or even a gun. But hey, it's a holster, so... just make sure to be open with security about what it is. I've probably been asked about it by security maybe three times, and it's never been a problem. In fact, under certain circumstances, I don't mind if people wonder what it is!

title: Barely fits 2 but it works
text: I have to really cram the two EpiPen‘s in there for them to fit, but it does work and my daughter likes how cute it is so she isn’t embarrassed to have to carry them around.

title: So far so good & it will fit my needs! Would recommend!
text:
I like the look at feel of this case. It easily holds two epi-pens with ease. This case I’ll take with me while traveling and keep the second one home. I haven’t had this case long so I can’t attest to the durability but I think it will hold up fine for my needs.
My daughter has a floral printed one and that is just as nice.
I would recommend these cases to people who are looking for a case to carry their epi-pens.

title: Improved product
text: All of the previous concerns about various product features seem to be fully addressed. I have been using this for a few weeks and none of the concerns previously listed like closing and the clip are there. In fact the clip now easily rotates to allow different positions and all of the manufacturing is sturdy. I'd recommend this.

title: Good value on a good product.
text:
Perfect. I needed something to hold two pens side by side, and provide decent protection. It does both.
An added bonus, it has a little clear slot to slide your prescription label into.

Love it. (I don't carry it on my belt, so I can't speak for the complaints about the clip. I carry it in my backpack, but now I and my friends know what to dig for if needed.)

text: I am very happy with this product overall.  The steam produced is immediate and effective.  My only complaint is, there is a small design flaw.  Hopefully the designers will read these reviews.  The lid that goes over the water compartment absolutely does not fit well, and does not lock into place.  It basically just rests there.  So it's very easy to accidentally knock it off with your hand while you hold it, or even for it to just fall off if you tip the thing too much to one side.  Very poorly designed cap.  It should fit securely and lock into place.  Fix that, folks, and this thing will be perfect.

title: FAKE C.A.T Tourniquet
text: DO NOT BUY!!! THIS IS A FAKE C.A.T TOURNIQUET!!! THESE ARE PRONE TO FAIL AND THE FAKE ONE'S BREAK... title: ONLY TO BE USED FOR TRAINING
text:
THIS IS NOT A LIFESAVING TOURNIQUET. It should not be used in a real-life trauma situation. The materials and construction are woefully sub-par. Parts of it started to break immediately. It LOOKS like many well-known tourniquets, but it is NOT on-par with the real thing.

That said, it's inexpensive and mimics the CAT-type ones close enough for training purposes. I used it at a class this past weekend and was pleased that I didn't need to put my real medical gear through adverse use conditions. A box of these would be fine for something like a Stop The Bleed course if budget is a concern.

Again, THIS IS NOT A LIFESAVING TOURNIQUET. Training use only.

title: Good product.
text: I hope I never need to use this, but it's sturdy and well-designed if I do.  If you are going to carry this, be sure to practice with it, including one-handed and in the dark.  You never know what the situation will be if you do need it.  Also, be sure to throw a permanent marker (sharpie) in with your kit so that you can mark the time that you put this baby on someone if you use it.

text: I think these are great for your average civilian med kit. Seems sturdy and tried mine pretty tight and no issues. Ordered one to try then ordered more bc I was impressed!!

title: Works but quality is low
text:
Gave the kit a test run, it works functionally.

However you can tell the product was very cheaply made; the plastic piece (in the photo below) was supper thin and sharp. While tightening, it will cut into your skin. If you apply the kit over clothing, it will be much more comfortable.
I am fully aware the purpose of this kit and it’s application. If god forbid you or someone you know need to actually use this kit, likely it’s a life or death situation, a little bit of “comfort” shouldn’t matter.
However again I want to voice that the materials are very cheaply made, the chance of pieces breaking off during tightening process is unlikely but do exist.

Besides this one I have also purchased a 16dollars kit from Amazon few months ago, in comparison that one had much higher quality over all.

In conclusion, this kit will work. If you want better quality get the 16dollars one on Amazon. If you want to save money and just want something to get by, get this it’s much better than nothing and have to tight up your limbs with random objects when your life is depending on it.

title: Stop the Bleed
text:

title: Excellent mask for glasses wearers
text:
The adjustable nose flap on this mask makes it really good at preventing my glasses from fogging up, I have several different types of masks with the built-in metal strip and this style is by far the best and most comfortable for me.

The mask also feels very high quality and it is pretty spacious on the inside in comparison to some of the other mask styles I've used. It even has a filter pocket!

title: Best cloth mask I’ve had for not fogging my glasses
text:
I like all it’s features. I found it very comfortable, easy to breath in, and the adjustable ear pieces I wonderful. I spent way too much money on masks since this whole pandemic started this one is working the best for me. I have the least problem with my glasses fogging with this mask and any of the other cloth masks I’ve had.
The wire strip at the bridge of the nose is wide enough and long enough to really make a custom fit to your face. Feels like it’s gonna hold up a long time.
That doesn’t mean you won’t have any fogging at all. When it was very very cold out and I went inside to warm buildings, I still had to use a little bit of anti-fog spray have my glasses. But it’s still better than every other mask I’ve tried.

title: Best, most comfortable mask on the market BAR NONE
text:
This awesome cloth mask fits perfectly. There is plenty of space to breathe, to speak and it fits over all the most important areas on your face. It is extremely comfortable! The nose bridge has a steel insert so you can "clamp" it down onto your nose. Fully covers your chin. It looks cool too. I also purchased a box of 30 PM 2.5 mask filters and the filter fits right into the open pocket on the inside so I have peace of mind.

I double-mask, so I wear my Graf Lanz over a KN95 - or a blue surgical mask. It easily fits over each and completely covers my inner mask.

I've had many people come up to me (well - at least 6 feet away!) and have to see what mask I am wearing from the label on the outside. This is a quality construction mask through and through. I'm very happy with it and will purchase more.

title: Practical and useful for delivering enema solutions directly into the colon
text:
I have used this colon tube a few times in the two weeks I've had it. I bought the largest size, 34 Fr, so that it wouldn't bend easily and kink although it is still flexible. With a little effort, I can get it through the sigmoid flexure to deliver the solution into the colon directly. The closed end with the side opening is a good design.

The tube fits easily and snugly over a standard rectal pipe. I liked it enough to purchase a second one.

title: Horrific
text: Can't say for any other size, but the fr34 is simply unusable.  Of course, different strokes and all that, and far be it from me to cast my thoughts to anyone else's anus/rectum/colon continuum, but as for me and mine, this is a rigid nightmare.  It was intimidating just to look at, like a freaky-long pink pinky finger, and turned out to be unworkable if you catch my drift.  Call me crazy, call me a hater, but I don't desire any alien-probe sensations in my descending colon. I'm trying the Gersons thing, what with a chronic pain issue.  Not working so far, but give it time.  Meantime I cannot use this purchase for its purported function, can't return it of course -- too short to tow a trailer with, or water the yard ... I'll mount it over the fireplace as a reminder to not believe every Amazon review when selecting colon catheters when trying to recapture my health.  Live and learn.

title: No more unpleasant surprises
text: This is the first time using a colon tube and was pleasantly surprised at how clean I felt afterwards. Have used the CleanStream silicone tube for years but never achieved the deep cleaning this product afforded. No more worry about unpleasant surprises when playing in the bedroom. I use it typically twice in a row with an enema bag until it runs clean; then have a glass of wine and repeat one last time for good measure.

title: Great for Coffee Enema / Gerson Therapy
text:
I've tried many tips and this one (FR22) works the best. On the Gerson Therapy 3-5 enemas a day are needed so finding a good tip is key.

1. it fits on all the enema bucket and bags that I've tried
2. the tip has round edges and works even for sensitive anus. most other brands fail here because they are either hard plastic with less than perfect edges or the tip opening is not well cut
3. lasts well over a month (3-5 uses/ day). typically dispose after 1 month not because it's worn out but just to be sanitary.

title: A good medical implement
text: "I recognize that many buy this product for . . . "alternate" uses. I have a spinal injury and due to the paralysis I must take an enema every day. I was using a 16 Fr. cath, but it took forever. So I bought this one. It is great. Gets well up in the colon for a good cleaning, and has a large enough opening that you can empty a 2 qt. bottle quickly."

Then just expel while tube is still in and push it a little higher.  twist it around so it get all sides.  Keep doing til water runs clear and u got a good amount of the tube up in you.  Works way better than Cleanstream silicone nozzle!

title: So Sad, Could have been great, Do not buy!
text: Ever spent more than you wanted to just because you thought you could get everything you needed all at once instead of building it yourself. The sad part of this product is that it could be great. The first aid products are a good start, and the backpack has padding with nice zippers. (Could use larger band-aids and gauze.)The trouble is that all the buckles and straps are made from super-slick material. (Unuseable, I have 30+ years of outdoor experience.) Strap on this pack, and it will simply slip off of you as all the straps come loose on their own. As if it was made by people that had pictures of a backpack but never used one. To use this product, you would need to replace all the buckles and straps or carry it in your arms like a pile of dirty Laundry. Buy your first aid gear separately and get a backpack that works. This one is a sad waste of money.

title: Very impressed. Meds and bag are much better quality than the pictures!
text:
I did a lot of research, and even spent an hour going though this product with my sister who is a medical nurse.

Not only does this check all the boxes and come with a great bag, but the quality of the medical materials is very good! I was originally hesitant, but after sorting the packages, and even breaking the seal on a few duplicate items to assess quality I've been very impressed. Many items are name brand, the rest are their "Lightning products" brand which seems to be very comparable. NONE of the items seem to be low quality or something I would not want to use in an emergency.

Bag is water resistant and is made of a plastic lined material, comfortable padding/adjustment when worn, Molle and sealing "military" zippers is a huge plus as well. (pic)

Although I feel most any 'normal' circumstance is fully covered and then some, I went the extra step and wanted to include treatment for more grizzly wounds such as working with chainsaws, machinery, and firearms. I added:

- MOST IMPORTANTLY a headlamp. 50% of earth's rotation is night, every medkit needs a hand-free light!
- Permanent Marker
- *Additional individual sterile gloves
- *Second Fishing Forceps
- Medline 35 Wide Skin Stapler
- SAM Bleeding Control Kit (Better for heavy bleeds and better *tourniquet)
- *SAM Chitosan Hemostatic Dressing (Better bandage for large wound clotting)
- *SAM Chest Seals (lung puncture "sticker" to seal/stabilize against collapsing)
- *Additional Israeli bandages for wrapping
- Petroleum bandages for continued care on healing wounds
- *Antiseptic Silvasorb Silver Hydrogel for continued care
- *Additional Israeli bandages
- Saline Wash

* Items in kit but purchased separately for additional quantity or better quality

Also to note. Everything will fit in the bag EXCEPT the Pulmonary Resuscitator, CPR Mask, Stethoscope, and Blood pressure cuff will NOT! You'll want a separate (similar sized) bag for those items as even when unpackaged they are too bulky and either don't fit at all, or would require displacing large amounts of the other items.

title: Okay if micro measures not required;  weirdly SLOW delivery from Amazon
text:
This is an OK product for generalized measures. See pic - product is on left side. NOT okay if you are administering- for example: 0.13 ml to a tiny animal. I do a fair amount of rehab and medical fostering of animals - and these syringes are fine for larger species like cats or large breed bunnies who - generally speaking - are OK if you pull for ex: 0.76 instead of 0 .75. Also OK for tiny guys so long as the substance administered is benign in the event too much is administered. But - for little guys who weigh only 1.5 - 2.2 pounds - the syringes are problematic for the administration of certain drugs because the measure marks for 100ths are even numbers only.
Also - don't count on speedy delivery. Occasionally, I'm swamped - taking care of 7 - 10 animals with various medical needs -- going through 12 - 20 syringes per day. Sometimes I slip up on ordering supplies. My last order on these syringes will take over a week to get to me. Sure - you can sterilize and re-use (not recommended), but what a hassle when you've got other meds to administer, SubQ fluids to give, injections, re-dressing wounds, changing out comfort pads, monitoring temps, etc... I'm finding another supplier because of this.

title: many uses with these electrodes
text: I got 23 uses out of these electrodes with my tens unit. Maintaining the electrodes and prepping your skin are both important to get as many uses as possible. I use these on both knees. My skin prep is to wet a paper towel and dampen my skin around the knee so the skin is glistening wet. Then I apply the pads. After the treatment ends, I return the pads onto the plastic they arrived on. Careful here! Once they're on the plastic, turn the plastic over and see if there are any air pockets. Press the pads more securely onto the plastic, otherwise the air pockets could reduce the longevity and effectiveness of the pads. Then, place the pads into the plastic bag and be sure to squeeze out as much air as you can before sealing the plastic bag.  Each of my treatment on the tens is 30 minutes long, set to Burst, Rate is 2.0, and Width is 50. These are pretty good pads and worked well for me. I've ordered them a 2nd time!

title: Just like OEM electrodes
text: The quality of these is great for $4. If you use it for a couple weeks and throw it out it's no big loss. I like the smaller electrodes because they are easier to place, and are easier to reuse. Make sure you wipe oil off your skin with alcohol before use or your skin oils will make the gel loose its adherence. Even when the gel is close to the end of it's life, it can be refreshed for a single use at a time with IceyHot/Bengay/or Aloe Gel. Basically moisture is what conducts the electrical currents.

text:
and it's been a challenge realizing and learning how to live with Diabetes, adjusting every aspect of my life and navigating the health care system. When I picked up my first insulin prescription pens, a once-a-day formulation, a box of 50 needles for the pens came with it. A day later I was prescribed a different type of insulin that I used several times throughout the day but did not come with the needle tips.

When I burned through the first 50 needles, I figured I'd just go pick up another box at the pharmacy but learned they needed to be prescribed for insurance otherwise are really expensive. The pharmacist recommended buying third party needles while we worked out the logistics for insurance.

I jumped on Amazon, did some research and landed on these because of price and reviews. They were delivered within 24 hours and fit my pens with no distinctions from the ones I had from the pharmacy. Since then, I've had two new insulin brands of pens. These needles have fit and worked with all of them.

I don't know if there is a "standard" all brands conform to, but they are compatible with the four different brands I've used. I'm very happy and am re-ordering as I write this review.

title: Followed the instructions as best as I can figure
text:
According to this device, as I sit here writing this, I have, apparently, already passed out long ago without drink, and, with only a half-cup of wine, it says that I am in danger of dying for the past hour.

I Just received it in the mail today. Followed the instructions as best as I can figure. I did a test first with no drinks. It registered me as .2+
Although I had not had any alcohol, I waited 20 minutes in case it was from what I ate at lunch - still .2+ (even higher than before)

I drank a few sips of wine, maybe 16% alc. I waited 15 ~ 20 min. It still said .2+ an that I should be almost passed out and severe memory loss.

I drank a little more - didn't even finish the cup - and waited over an hour without eating or even drinking water in order to not skew the results and to test it said that I now am .3+ and that I am in danger of dying. If that happens, please alert my next of kin as to why.

UPDATE:

Day two and I am getting the same dubious results. It told me I was .2 in the morning, (down from .5+ the night before a seven hour sleep and nothing to drink for hours since i was apparently supposed to be dead after my half-drink. This time I am using it in combination with other track your drinking app I found on google play that lets me input what and how much I drank and estimates you BAC (no blowing). The results from this app (although estimations) seem much more realistic in terms of the effects.

I will give this a few more tires, but since there is no way to accurately test it other than buy a few other brand devices and test them all together it is quite frustrating.

title: Accurate and Can Save Lives!
text:
I once was a juror on a drunken driving case and the judge actually said, "I want to make it clear. It is not illegal to drink and drive; it is illegal to drive drunk or impaired". Well, it doesn't take much alcohol to get you legally drunk or impaired.

This tiny little device (2" X 3" X 0.5") is a complex breathalyzer that uses your iPhone for results! It only takes less than a minute to `pair' with your iPhone (you must download the free BACtrack app. It will ask for credit card info, but is not charged).
First thing to do is set the settings to your gender and weight for accuracy. Note that females have fewer enzymes to break down alcohol and certain races have even less. Check Wikipedia or GOOGLE for this information.

Open the app, and when it says `take a reading', a clock appears and gives you one minute to prepare. Simply `BLOW NOW!' by taking a steady deep blow into the analyzer while watching the eight blue bars fill up - then you stop. There is a slight `click'. The test results are shown on your phone via a large number, such as 0.004 (which means it is likely you are very sober). Click 'OK' and you are shown a `graph' that indicate the times between `blows' and your alcohol level. 0.08 is legally drunk and you should test again in fifteen minutes.

There is also an option to get a "Dose-Specific Effect" of your alcohol level with suggestions. It is also very important to wait at least fifteen (15) minutes to test after your last drink, cigarette or food consumption.
You can `tag' a drink for future use in the computer storage, like a beer, glass of wine, liquor, etc. You can add a photo of that time period (although this would be more appropriate if you were at a party sharing the device and getting a shot of a 0.18% drinker looks like. The device does come with three plastic washable mouthpieces. There is a tab for notes. There is also a `share' button which lets you share your results on Facebook, text it, or tweet it. Now come on! Close out the program and your entire previous tests are stored. There is a system called `Zeroline' which estimates how long it will take your Blood Alcohol Content (BAC) to return to 0.00% based on your last test result.

My results the first time:
I enter `Male' and `195 pounds' at 8:00pm on an empty stomach; 4 ounces; Vodka with soda. This is a typical bar mix.
After one hour my BAC was 0.10. Over the legal limit. The second hour I drank a 2 oz. drink and waited an hour. My BAC was 0.065.

So 6 ounces of vodka on a fairly empty stomach with the `time to sobriety' (0.00%) would happen around 2:00am. This was interesting information. It's a pricey unit, but not anywhere near the over $10,000 it is estimated, to deal with being busted drunk driving. Drive safely!

Just didn't realize how small this BACtrack was until I opened the box... posted a photo to show size in hand.

1.6 oz on digital scale.

Comes with nice little soft pouch to protect it a bit, will fit in your pocket or purse without problem.
But should come with a wrist or neck strap in my opinion as the conditions it will be used under could promote dropping it.

Seems to work just fine and paired up via bluetooth without any trouble, iPad / iPhone app does everything needed to "analyze" drinking trends over time... BUT
I do wish they would have made it with a readout right on the unit so it could be used as a quick check without the need to connect with bluetooth every time.

Also wish they would have/could have made it compatible with Android devices also... there are as many, if not more, Android owners/users as there are Apple these days I believe.

text: This face shield is built of well-made, sturdy plastic and is definitely reusable. There is a rubber attachment piece that fits over the forehead plate for a comfortable and snug fit. The removable strap in the back is a nice touch to accommodate the various head sizes. The only problem I had was the design of the attachment points for the side arms. These are designed inward instead of flat.  After a short period of time, this design caused pressure points on my head and became uncomfortable. I was able to heat the side strap and straighten them, as they do with reading glasses. With the side strap straight, the fit improved considerably. I am able to wear the face shield around the house without discomfort. With a wider strap on the sides and back, this would improve the feeling that the face shield is too heavy in the front. It is unfortunate that we are having to purchase face shields at all, but I am appreciative to the folks who make the effort. I would recommend this product.

title: easy to use, easy to clean, smaller capacity means no long sitting of water, lovely warm mist
text:
Humidifiers save my hair, my skin, my sinus' during our long, cold, dry Northern winters. I tend to use a cool mist humidifier in my bedroom (since I sleep with a husband and two large dogs and it gets really warm in there), and I prefer a warm mist humidifier everywhere else- warm just feels so nice. I sometimes boil water on my stove to help raise the humidity, but since I am not sitting next to the stove, I tend to carry a humidifier around with me from room to room. I have an old Vicks one that still functions, but I like the style of this one as it is easier to clean and set up wherever I am at. Takes up a bit less space.

I think I measured it at being 9-10" wide at widest point, and about same in height. I currently use it most often next to me on the couch when I settling down for the evening (eat dinner, watch tv, veg out on couch with dogs). If I am going to be in my home office for long periods of time, i have moved it into there as well. If this continues to be a good one for me, I may just purchase another so I don't have to remember to move it around. I bet my dogs and my cats like it too since we have not been shocking each other as much when we touch.

Water capacity is just a half gallon. I can keep it going for several hours on low, and I didn't keep track of how long on high. But low setting is supposed to be 13 hours. I would say that seems accurate. Overall,. I don't mind refilling it as I am not trying to use it for days on end. I actually prefer the slightly smaller capacity because it kinda grosses me out to use water that has been sitting for a long time. SO this is kinda perfect for me. But that is really just a preference thing.

You will get greatest increase in humidity by using this in a small space, or if using in a larger space, then sitting next to it so you reap the benefits.

One more thing.. It has an option for additives- a medicine cup/vapor pad tray. I haven't had to use that yet, fortunately :)

I haven't any complaints or concerns at this time. If I experience anything notable, I will be back to update.

title: Easy to Use / Clean, No Filter / No Fuss
text: We bought a big fancy humidifier last year, it seemed like a good deal.  Later we realized the filters were expensive & hard to find.  Also, it was nearly impossible to clean when the filter spread mold to the inside with in a couple of weeks.  This crane warm myst humidifier is a completely different story.  No filter, easy to clean, big enough for our living room, a life saver when cold season hit.  I’m honestly very happy & excited that this worked out.  This is proof that simplicity is often the best design.  Great humidifier, 5 stars.

title: What relief this humidifier was able to offer was cut short by the small tank.
text:
+ Produces steam within 2-3 minutes; steady flow
+ Works well when you are suffering from a head cold or nasal congestion
+ Small unit; doesn’t take up a lot of space
+ Portability and ease of cleaning

± Price seems rather hefty, especially considering the tank size
± 0.5 gallon does not go a long way: works great during woken hours, but does not last 8+ hours at night
± Constructed out of plastic that is relatively “thin”; don’t drop
± Be careful with eucalyptus-based bar if you own pets (more mentioned below)

- No way to control the direction of the steam

------------------------------------------

The first day of use, I filled the tank 3/4th’s of the way. I figured this would last me the whole night, as my cold mist humidifier does fine on even less. I was awoken, however, to a shrill “empty” beeping indicator at 5am. This was a mere 5 hours after first fill - definitely wasn’t happy. No, I was not using the highest setting (depicted by 2 steam lines), so perhaps I’m just an anomaly.

Anyway, I appreciate that the product itself works. Steam was produced within 2-3 minutes, more often within 1, and it was steady enough to where I felt the effects during my congested state. You’re not able to control the direction of the steam though, so this was rather unfortunate.

The product itself is made of plastic with a metal heating plate area. It’s not sturdy material at all, and feels rather delicate. Realistically, this will survive perhaps 3 drops, if even that - I won’t be testing that any time soon though.

Now, this tidbit may or may not be relevant to you, so skip if you don’t own pets. I don’t know if I’m perpetuating a scare either, but I wanted to add this in nonetheless. I was lying in bed with the provided eucalyptus mint bar sitting in the catch tray as the steam rose. As I was laying down, I noticed how strong the scent was, therefore decided to quickly check if it would affect my dogs. Well, it’s a good thing that I confirmed as I discovered that these vapors are known for causing seizures in dogs…

I’m not one to normally believe everything I read online, so I dug a little deeper, where I continued to come across mixed reviews. Most of the reviews favored heavily towards avoiding eucalyptus-based vapor products when around dogs though, so I immediately ceased use.

At $44.99 (on sale), this product does not feel worth it. It only offered 5 hours of relief, so while I may have received a faulty product, it still didn’t perform as long as one would expect. Otherwise, this does produce a nice stream of steam, so does aid with some nasal relief.

title: Simple to use, love the fact that its warm mist and could use essential oil in tray
text:
I got this because I have never come across a warm humidifier with the option of adding essential oil (which is what I always wanted) I usually use a diffuser/humidifier when someone in our house is sick, and I like to add eucalyptus or something along those lines for (stuffy noses because it helps them sleep better, and moisture helps with dry air.) I feel like the warm humidifier is more effective with opening up nasal passages. The size is pretty convenient would fit nicely on a nightstand and hold enough water (half gallon) to run for 13 hours. Mine came looking used because there were several dirty looking spots on it (pictures). I filled it up today because my daughter is currently sick with what sounds like croup. You simple unscrew the bottom of the tank and fill it up (I noticed there is no line that says the max) so i filled it up to the brand name. It took a couple minutes to warm up and then it started to shoot out the warm (kinda hot) vapor. There is only one button so it's very easy to operate- the button gives you 3 different options: low, high, or off. I love the tray feature for the essential oil vapor that and the warm air are the main reasons why I decided to get it! It's also pretty quiet, just kind of sounds like a very low heater fan. It's easy to clean and doesnt require filters either.
Overall happy and working out great so far.

Beware! I have four pair of PowerStep ProTech orthopedic inserts and love them. They are great for my problems with plantar fasciitis, high arches, and over pronation. I ordered two new pair from a different seller and noticed some major differences immediately. The new inserts (1) have a rounded bottom instead of the molded heel; (2) have a shallower heel cup; and (3) have a smaller arch support.

Seeing these major differences, I then found a number of minor differences including: (4) the U.S. Patent number is missing; (5) the labeling is faded; and (6) a ridge line is detectable under the arch.

I looked at the packaging and a small label has been applied to the box that states; "New, Improved PowerStep." I can say, with no hesitation, these new inserts are NOT IMPROVED over the originals. They appear much more cheaply made and do not provide the deep cup and high arch that the original inserts have. Either these are cheap knockoffs or PowerStep has changed their design. I'm not sure which but I am sending these two new pair back. I will try attaching photos but since this is my first time to post a review, I'm not sure if I'll be successful.

title: Great support for the price.
text: I'm a podiatrist and I recommend these all of the time to patients. They are second only to a great custom orthotic. These are generally ideal for people with a mildly flat foot to high arch that need a little extra support. They work best in an athletic shoe with a removable insole. I wear them in my shoes and boots that I get very dirty so that I don't ruin my custom orthotics (which I still prefer personally). I do have some patients that prefer these over their custom orthotics. You can't beat the price. Expect them to last 6-12 months depending upon how much you wear them and in what conditions. If they get wet and muddy a lot, they wear out more rapidly. They are fat superior to most other premade supports although SOLE supports are great too (just a little less cushioned).

title: Makes crappy shoes awesome!
text:
I was in Zimbabwe last summer doing a combination of vacationing and relief work. I only brought a pair of tennis shoes and loafers with me. We were going hiking, and I didn't have boots or anything to get muddy in. So I bought a pair of boots from the only place nearby at the time. The place was rather shady. It was more of a shack than an actual store. None of the shoes had insoles. They'd been removed, and no explanation was offered. I reluctantly bought a pair of Champion boots as they were the cheapest pair the man would sell me.

Many miles and blisters later, I ended up back in the United States with these pain in the foot boots. I didn't wear them again for close to a year. I decided it was time to buy some insoles and give them another shot considering the amount of money I'd already sunk into them. I did my usual Amazon search for a highly rated and well priced product. These Powerstep insoles came up, and I'm so glad I bought them. I wear size 11, so I bought the 11-11 1/2 Men's. I now love the boots. I wish I had these insoles back when I really needed them in Zimb. O well. Now I'm happy :)

title: This seems to be a knock-off, but the pic on packaging looks almost the same
text:
BEWARE!!!
Although the outside packaging is made to look almost the same as the REAL DEAL, this product is NOT the same as the one available via the doctor's office, and of course for a higher cost. It seems this product is a knock-off. The curves and the lift of the sole at various angles are different than the original, which then also changes the structure, specs, and therefore the ACTUAL INTENDED SHAPE of the Sole itself. I missed the Return window and therefore am stuck with it, but will NOT use it. This product might work for few, but since it is NOT the SAME spec as the original, it will create more foot problems for others... THEREFORE BEWARE...!!! It might be worth buying it from the doctor's office for a higher cost and getting the REAL DEAL!!

title: Outstanding Orthotic insoles
text: I am on my feet a lot and as a former athlete I always purchased top of the line insoles. These are by far the best I have ever purchased. Recommended by my doctor, they are better than the $400.00 custom insoles I had made. I highly recommend them.

title: Happy Feet 👣
text: These were recomended by a podiatrist, & I'm so happy I found them online.  I have severe arthritis on tops of both feet along with bunions.  The doc cautioned that I may need to ease into them, but I've been wearing them constantly since.  I place old pairs in shoes I don't wear often for yard work, winter boots, etc.  I highly recommend!

title: Finally - an insert that works for me!
text: I've ordered a dozen different inserts online and sent them all back. I have tried EVERY insert in the stores: walk-fits, goodfeet, drscholls, sof soles, etc. but none of them worked for me. I have 13 screws in my foot (calcaneus fracture in 2001). These inserts fit well and feel great. These have more of a lift under my arch and are comfortable. These don't cause any pronation or supination. I plan to buy a pair for every shoe!

title: Relief for your feet
text: I can't live without my Powerstep inserts.  I remove the inner soles in my shoes and insert these.  They help so much if you have plantar facitisis or posterior tibia tendon dysfunction.

title: Beautiful socks, but...
text: I adore the Bright Majik print on these socks. If you need a bit of compression, why not have fun with it? The compression is light, so if you need something stronger you'll need to go elsewhere. The only thing that kept me from giving it 5 stars is the fact that it left an indentation, a "ring' if you will, around my calf at the very top of the sock. Compression socks really shouldn't do that. I also bought the "Lace" pair, though, which do not seem to have the same problem. The fit is fine and they seem surprisingly sturdy, though I've only worn them a few times. I do hand wash them, which should help. Definitely worth it for a bit of fun!

title: Just love these socks but they do have one small issue
text: These socks are great. The fabric is soft, smooth, lovely; feels really nice next to my skin. I love how colorful & fun these compression socks are because all I've found up until now were just drab tan, black or white stockings that looked hideous. Just because I have peripheral vascular return issues with my lower extremities (feet, calves) doesn't mean I want to look so frumpy wearing the traditional compression hose. These are so cute, bright & colorful. The only downside is that I am wearing these due to leg swelling & when my calves are real swollen (which is often unfortunately), the design on some of these socks gets stretched out, causing you to lose the very thing that makes these so pretty. The design stretches enough to where it looks blurry to completely lost on some designs & not so colorful. This hasn't happened on all the socks I've purchased from this maker, (I have about 6 pairs), but definitely on some. If you're on the thin side or don't experience much swelling, this probably won't be a problem at all. A solution to this would be if the company made them in a couple of sizes, like small & large.

title: Liked them, but didn't fit
text: I have pretty large calves (even after losing considerable weight) and they did not fit.  They were very pretty and wish they had.

title: Cool and comfortable.
text: These socks are so cute and comfortable they almost make up for having to wear compression socks! Plenty of support, and they stay up nicely.

title: Support Hose for the Wild at Heart
text:
My friend gave me a pair of these (in a different pattern) for my 70th birthday. She called them psychedelic support hose. I loved the pattern and the support so I immediately looked to see if I could find them on Amazon. I have had varicose veins since I was in my 30s and these compare to the support in regular ugly compression hosiery. I will be ordering more of these I only wish there were more patterns eligible for Amazon Prime Shipping. I always receive compliments on them. I am hesitant to try the next level of compression since the 8-15 seems just right for me and are not overly tight at the top. In case it helps anyone decide on the compression level they want to try, I am 5 foot, 5.5 inches and 115 pounds.
UPDATE: As of now, I have about 5 pair of Celeste Stein stockings. They have all been good. The Austin Powers pattern is my favorite. I have worn them so much they have faded out some but are still quite attractive.
