title: All that up and down causes hose to want to pull down which can be annoying not to mention having to pull them back up ...
text: I work at a big box retail store and am on my feet 6 - 8 hrs a day on concrete.  At the age of 53 the concrete was causing my legs to severely ache.  Then I remembered something about how nurses often wear support hose to help with their legs.  With my job, there is a lot of squatting, kneeling and sometimes sitting on the floor.  All that up and down causes hose to want to pull down which can be annoying not to mention having to pull them back up every time you go to the rest room; which can be quite a task during the summer months.  So I got on amazon and started looking for something better and found the compression socks.  I had forgotten about them.  These work great.  The compression is just enough to keep my legs from aching (only from the knee down ached -- not my thighs).  They are not hard to get on, but it can be a little difficult pulling them off.  But once you've worn them a couple times they start to loosen up and pull off easier.  I usually wear them under my regular socks -- especially during winter to keep my legs from getting cold.  In my work environment you don't wear dresses, so the knee high compression socks are perfect.  I am constantly on the move, in the store, and they do not slip down.  I have more trouble with keeping the regular socks up.  Compression helps with my legs -- absolutely no more ache.  A lot of people will not consider compression hose or socks because they associate that with old age.  But hey, I am old, and I choose not to suffer unnecessary discomfort.  I have a lot of energy and have always moved at a quick pace; these socks help me to enjoy my job and maintain the high energy life I am used to.

title: FUN compression socks
text: Why have to wear those boring orthopedic socks, if you can have a little fun with these designs.  Midnight Lace is actually quite pretty.

title: Top elastic too tight
text: Nice product, but the top is too constrictive and leaves an ugly mark on your legs. I'm NOT heavy, (5'4" and 120 pounds) but my legs bulge above the tops. NOT a good look. I think they should do better ...

title: Not for me
text: These socks are really cute, well made, but they definitely are NOT moderate compression hose. I'm an RN, and these socks offer compression comparable to light/thin TED hose. The reason I rated them a 3 star is because very shortly after I put them on, they begin to slide/slip down my leg . So, if you already have thin legs, they might be what you want. But for us older gals, with not so thin legs, (& I'm  NOT even talking heavy legs here), I'd look at something else, like perhaps Nobee socks.

title: best purchase of medical school
text:
I'm a medical student, so I sit on a hard chair for hours every day in lecture. This seat cushion is quite literally saving my ass, preventing the coccyx, hip, and lower back pain that was plaguing me by the end of first year. It's form does a good job of distributing the pressure. I also like that you can zip off the front 1/3 for shallow chairs.

One warning: do not buy this cushion if you are much bigger than a US women's size 10-12. There is a plastic form inside, and it will probably jab you where it curves up on the sides.

title: A back-saver wherever you sit
text: If you have been experiencing lower back pain after being seated for some time, this attractive and comfortable portable seat could be just the answer.  I had been experiencing lower back problems after visiting friends in the country.  Suspecting that my pain was being caused by their dining room chairs, where we watched TV for hours on end, I brought along the Obus Forme Seat on my last visit.  No more pain!  The seat comes in a handy little plastic tote bag with a handle for carrying, and you can zip off the front segment of the seat to fit shallower chairs.

title: Truck Driver's Dream
text: I bought this seat for my husband --- he is a 6'2, 185 Lb. over the road truck driver (anyone who knows what trucking is like knows what it does to you). He had tried other seats with limited success and he loves this one. I knew about the Obus because I've used one for over 15 years in my Subarus (not known for their comfortable seating) and it is still in acceptable shape. I bought it originally because I'm a small person who rattles around in most vehicles and had a lower back problem, and it has made long distance driving without pain possible. It also goes well with the lower back rest, but can be used very effectively without it. It has an inner form that is far and away better than other seats I have tried. Don't even bother looking at other brands. This is the best seat on the market.

title: Good support for my Honda CR-V
text: After some lower back issues, I was in the market for seat and lumbar support cushions to help with longer car rides in my Gen 3 Honda CR-V. There are dozens on the market and I've tried most of them from cheap no-name brands to the expensive temperp**** and brooksto** brands. I found the cheaper ones were either too thin and non-supportive or way too firm and no give to them. I also found the more expensive ones comfy with good support, but a bit too thick and pushed me either too high up or too far forward in my seat. I turned to amazon and reviews from others which helped me settle on trying this Obus seat. Right away I found it fit almost perfectly in my CR-V's driver seat in both depth and width. After driving around for a few days, it provided the right amount of padding, and while I'm about an inch or so higher I'm nowhere near the head liner (I'm a bit under 6 feet tall). I did not experience feeling any wires or seams as others have mentioned. Finally I noticed that I no longer needed a separate lumbar cushion, the Obus seat raised me just enough to get more support from the standard seat. I also spoke with my physical therapist and she mentioned that Honda's bottom seat tends to be low and agreed just the seat cushion alone should do the trick. So if you are in the market to improve the comfort of your Honda's seat, give the Obus seat a try.

title: Great seat cushion to accompany the back support
text:
Great firm seat cushion. It stays in place well, and is a good complement to the Obus Forme back support device. You have to play around with it to get things at the perfect spot, being that they're two completely separate pieces.

The front section zips off (see in the photo there are three sections). If you're short, give it a try both ways, first with the entire cushion, then later with the one section removed. This will help you decide which way is best for you personally.

The only complaint I can think of is that the back support and the seat cushion should be offered as a set so that someone doesn't have to purchase the items separately.

title: Strangely Wonderful
text:
I drive cross country and would always get shooting pains down my right leg after about 7 hours. I ordered a few different seat cushions from Amazon, but returned them immediately. They didn't even work in town, no way I was taking them on the road. I was sure this one would be the same, especially because I couldn't feel any difference when I put it on the seat of my 06 Honda Civic. It raised my seat about an inch, but I'd tried that adjustment before with no improvement so had no expectations.
Imagine my surprise when there was no pain after 7 hours, or 9, or 11. Nor the next day of 500 miles. This is a keeper!
Some reviewers have complained about the hard plastic base. I don't even feel it, and I'm not a delicate flower in the seat region.
It does slip a bit, but shoving the two straps through the crack between the seat and seat back helps a lot.
And it's not hot. That is worth a 6th star.

title: Not as comfortable as I would have liked
text: After sitting in my recliner too much and triggering a bout of back pain (that later turned into a severely herniated disc) I purchased the Obus Ultra Forme backrest for added support.  I was so happy with the backrest that I decided that adding the seat was called for.  It unfortunately turned out to be fairly uncomfortable.  The support was pretty good, and the problem might have been that it was too small for my recliner, but I ended up returning it.  I'm 6'4", 200lbs, so maybe I don't have enough built in padding, but regardless, I was disappointed in the seat after being so happy with the backrest.

title: Seat bought for sciatica issue
text:
My husband was having a leg issue with his right driving leg on long trips (over an hour) when a pain would flare up (not every time but enough to be annoying and noticeable) that he would then place his right fist under the leg to relieve the extension of the muscle by shortening it in the space - not an ideal solution to maintain this positioning for hours! I bought this cushion over others because it has plastic embedded inside skeleton to make it structurally firmer, essentially recreating his hand position. He only uses it in the car because car seats are notoriously uncomfortable and ill-suited for long trips. (He also has a long commute to work every day.), especailly Subarus, which he likes for the 4-wheel drive and wagon features.

This cushion was tried for just a week and he has remarked on how much more comfortable the car seat is now with the cushion versus without it. The pain hasn't flared up at all, although the longest trip so far has only been 2 hours, but still it's a good sign that the seat is working for my intended purpose - to keep the pain from occuring in the first place.

I would have rated it 5 stars, but am holding off because it's only been a week and I want to see how the cushion holds up over more time. $55 is a bit pricey for a seat cushion, so I reserve the highest rating because with a higher price comes a higher expectation on duration, which time will tell on that aspect.

I would recommend this cushion for this purpose largely for the internal formed plastic structure piece. This was the only seat cushion I found with this valuable feature, which appears to be a solution for warding off the sciatic issue,.

title: Had more SI (sacroiliac) Joint pain when using the seat/back combination that without it.
text: I can only rate the Obus Forme Ergonomic Seat for its short term performance in the purpose for which I purchased it after several recommendations.  I bought this product to relieve stress on my SI (sacroiliac) joint in which I have developed sacroilitis or the inflamation of the SI joint, and the low-back pain associated with it.  I found several recommendations across the Internet stating that this product and the associated Ergonomic low-back seat back could help.  I received the seat and the back one day and tried them out in my computer chair at home and was very uncomfortable.  The next day I tried them together in my car seat and in addition to the seat adjustments I had to make for the extra height and thickness, I was in more pain after my drive to work WITH the cushions, than without them.  I returned them both the very next day, and bought a 2" memory-foam dining chair cushion for $13.00 which works better for my pain. I'm sure it probably would suit other purposes, but definitely not for my SI Joint pain!

title: Protect your back
text: I was a little skeptical about the Obus seat,  I thought I just needed the back rest.  However the seat helps to keep you in the correct position.

title: The Very Best
text: There is only one reason you would want such a wedge cushion: to help you to more perfect balance while sitting (not to cushion the tush) and thus perhaps to reduce back pain and stress you might experience.  Thus there are only 2 requisites: (1) It must have an angle sufficient to tilt the body forward and (2) it must be firm enough so that such an adequate angle is not lost when putting the body's heavy weight on it.  I have tried all of the wedge cushions offered anywhere and they all fail this test --- with the exception of the Core 5405.  It is as close to perfect as it gets.  I would love to see a version that is covered in fabric, since the foam can show signs of edge wear over time if it is not covered.

title: Recommended By My Physical Therapist
text:
My physical therapist got me started using wedges. I have low back pain and an unstable SI joint, and this wedge (despite my skepticism), really does place your pelvis in a more neutral position that takes some pressure off the spine.

This particular one is pretty firm.....I prefer firm, but it was even too firm for me until I put it on the floor and stepped on it a few times. Now it's perfect.

I do wish the back was more rounded to match the contour of most seatbacks. The curvature of the bucket seat in my car meant it was sitting out a good 2" from the seat back. Took care of that by rounding off the edges of the wedge with a knife.

title: Works great as a booster pad
text: I bought this because, as a very short person (5'0"), I could not get comfortable in my car. The seats slope down from front to back, and I felt I was always sitting in a hole, and could not see properly. If I raised the seat, the front would then be too high for me to reach the pedals. I figured a wedge cushion would be the answer. Memory foam would not work, as it would compress too much, I would need rigid foam, and this is definitely rigid. Well, I have to say, it is absolutely perfect. I now have great visibility, my posture is better, and it is actually pretty comfortable. I was actually able to wedge it into the back of the seat. A very cheap answer to a very annoying problem.

title: Very Good Cushion
text: I looked at several of these. This one is simply high density foam with no cover. It supports my weight (165 lbs) well. It is very light and can pack easily. Also not too large to use in my car. I am a chiropractor and I use these and recommend a wedge seat cushion to all my patients. You cant' beat this at the price.

title: It's growing on me...
text: I ordered this wedge cushion to use in my car for my bucket seat. This was the only wedge I found that was close to the right size. All the other ones I've tried are way too wide, and just kind of sit on top of the side wings of my seat, as the base of the seat is pretty narrow. The wedge almost fit- it is still a little too wide, but I figured maybe after some use the sides would give a little. When I first sat on this cushion in my car, I felt like I was sitting on a wooden board or something. It put a little more pressure on my tail bone, which I was afraid would become an issue, as I already have back and sciatic problems. Since the cushion gave me a little boost, I had to adjust my seat lower. I was certainly more comfortable sitting at this angle with my pelvis tilted upwards a bit. I just wished it wasn't as firm or  wished it had a memory foam type of feel. Anyway, because I was so uncomfortable without a cushion, I stuck with it. I seem to be "breaking it in" a bit, as it doesn't feel as awkward now. I'm hoping it will get even more comfortable with time. One other thing that would've been nice is if this cushion had a cover, to keep it clean. Overall, I think it was worth a try and will keep using it for now.

title: Solved my back pain while driving
text: I purchased this to relieve low back pain while driving. It fits well in the driver seat of my 2014 Honda Civic. I use a pillow case as a cover. It is supportive while still having a good cushioning "give."  My back pain was relieved almost immediately.  This is the perfect solution for me to get my hips level with my knees, which per my MD and physical therapist is what I need to relieve pain in my low back.  I have been using for about 6 weeks and it is holding up "like new." This is a great price point for a product contributing a lot to my quality of life. Thank you.

title: Works well on car seat to flatten out the slope.
text: I bought this to place under a dog booster seat that helps raise my dog up and holster him in for safety. The seat sloped backwards from the front, so this wedge cushion helped straighten it out to make the whole seat more level. Worked well, and good price.

title: Used these to block stuff from falling between the mattress ...
text: Used these to block stuff from falling between the mattress and headboard.  Also used one to prop myself up in wheelchair.

title: this wedge is already mashed down it is now a cushion
text: after using 2 months the wedge has flattened on my chair at the office and I weigh 110- not good!

title: Few months in and still going strong
text: I was expecting this to go flat overtime like other seat cushions I have but the foam is surprisingly durable. Slip on a pillow case and it makes a great cushion

title: Idea is there, design is not
text:
Purchased this for my husband's boot (broken foot). His boot is open toe but work demands closed toe and this was the best/cheapest optionI could find.

The idea itself is ingenious, but the thought put into creating it is a bit lax.

The plastic is not at all bendable, my husband put it over an open stove to heat it up and bend it so it's not so large.

The openings on the side are just that,
large openings; your foot is not really protected from any elements, just possibly other people's sneakers, table legs, etc.

The picture shows a full length white got length paper behind it, and the description sneakily portrays that it sticks to the bottom of the boot (underneath the soft part). That is not the case, the toe guard does not have that white part to stick it in the entire length of the boot (which would have made more sense, honestly) it comes with just the toe guard attached to a short piece of plastic about the length of the toe guard itself. It does have the sticky part on it, but i have no clue wether its sticky enough or not (easily fixed with Velcro tape if its not sticky enough, i would assume) although I was a bit bummed about that, hubby said its fine.

To anyone needing a closed toe boot, i searched. I did not find any other product that I deemed comparable. This is what we did to make sure the boot was okayed by work:

A) put it under a hot stove/torch it to fit more flush with your boot. We did this on all 3 sides (2 sides and top)

B) either ghetto rig it like us, or come up with a fancier version; we simply pulled a black sock over the whole thing once it sat flush with the boot, slit an opening where the toes are supposed to sit, and slid the whole shebang under the soft part of the boot, tucking the rest of the sock all the way to the back of the boot. Unless someone is really REALLY concentrating on the boot, no one will notice. It won't hide your foot from the elements, but it being summer right now, that wasn't our main issue, so weather/ rain proofing wasn't a necessity. (Beeswax rubbed onto whatever fabric you use then melted on with a hair dryer might do the trick)

In conclusion...

Pros:
Great idea
Does guard your toes a bit
Sturdy plastic material

Cons:
Large (husband wears 12.5 and this thing before molded resembled a clown shoe on him)
Falsely advertised
Cumbersome
Does not protect your feet from much other than other peoples feet/toe stubbing; beware of clumsy chicks in high heels.

Is this the best product out there? Unfortunately, yes.

Will it get the job done? Kinda.

Although it's a bit cumbersome, it really is a great idea and after tinkering around with it a bit, will get the job done. It's a good base to start at, but you will likely have to put a little elbow grease into customizing it to your specs.

Hope that helps!

title: Functional, but not great
text: I ordered the large Darco toe guard to fit in my men's large Darco square-toed surgical shoe after toe surgery to provide some additional protection during recovery. As far as the primary goal of the product: it absolutely covers and protects the toe. However, I have a few complaints: first, it is enormous and looks fairly ridiculous hanging way off the front of the shoe. It is in no way mold-able by hand as advertised. I would recommend other buyers to be sure you get the smallest size you think you can get away with. It also does not fit into the square-toed shoe well at all; the insole won't go back down into the shoe with the toe-guard in place. I just put the guard in when I'm around the house to protect from the dog and my little ones, and not when I'm in public because it is uncomfortable and unsightly. I would probably buy the product again just because it is functional and fits the Darco shoe, but would try a smaller size (perhaps the women's size?) if I thought I could make it fit.

title: Broken Toe? You need this!
text:
I broke my big toe this summer and was looking for something that offered a little more protection then just the boot the orthopedic surgeon gave me, which was completely soft and unprotected on top. (Why on earth there isn't a protective toe on those ugly boots I'll never know. You already look like Frankenstein in that crazy boot, you might as well have some protection while you're at it.)
I found that lifting the foam of the boot and placing this under with a little extra glue the perfect way to complete my "Frankenstein" look! It also provided me some MUCH needed protection while on Vacation.

Several times I was grateful to be wearing the boot because of oblivious tourists bumping in to me. I was very glad I had this and it was completely worth the money!

title: Perfect
text:
Amazing device. Exactly what I needed to protect my toe with a k-wire sticking out the front. This "womens square" is actually the perfect size for a "large" darco square surgical shoe. I also tried the "mens large" version, and it is ridiculously huge. I will note that my foot was bandaged, not it a big cast, so if you have a cast you might need the bigger clearance offered by the mens size.

This armor should be standard issue in hospitals when they give you a boot post toe surgery. Open toed boots are are worthless for protection by themselves - they only keep your foot from bending (to protect wires, pins or bones).

title: Great protection for post op bunion and hammertoe surgery
text: Great protection for post op bunion and hammertoe surgery. I have a steel pin sticking out of my second toe and needed something to protect it while wearing my boot. This works perfectly! My doctor s had never seen one before and were very impressed and enthusiastic about it.

title: Kept the safety guys at bay.
text: This is NOT a safety toe cap. It offers no actual toe/foot protection that is required by OSHA for many blue collar jobs. I had to wear a walking boot for four weeks and could not take that much time off of work, I bought this and attached it to my ortho bolt. I believe having the visible toe guard kept the safety team satisfied, at least from a distance.

title: Saved my toes!
text: [[VIDEOID:ff3f42f699b3aace6cf70c6eca026a1e]] Anyone having hammertoe surgery, this is a MUST! I have protected the wires sticking out of my toes countless times! Between the dogs, blankets, drawers etc. Toe saver!

title: Great product
text: I was skeptical when I purchased it, but I am so thankful I did.  It gave great protection to my foot after surgery.  It adheres very well to the boot and was easy to apply.

title: Awesome product gives peace of mind and protection
text:
After hammer toe surgery on both feet, having these protectors inserted in the open-toe, surgery-recovery shoes saved me from stubbing or bumping my repaired toes which had pins sticking out beyond the end of the toes. These toe guards kept blankets away, prevented bumps and provided peace of mind during recovery knowing my vulnerable toes would be protected from any accidental contact.
I was very thankful to have these.

title: Guards toes with pins
text: The only thing that needs improvement is a better adhesive to keep the guard in place. It is really helpful to me by protecting my toe with a pin in it after hammer toe surgery

title: It works after 2.5 weeks.
text: I had a very bad nerve pain on my neck which started 8 weeks ago. The first month the pain was very bad, and it moved from left to the right side. I couldn't sit for 30 minutes, and working at the computer bought so much pain it was hard for me to focus. Even though I was consciously taking hourly breaks throughout the day and doing mild stretches, I could barely manage my daily activity, but the pain did not reduce too much. I ordered this product from Amazon marketplace, and started using it 2.5 weeks ago. I followed the instructions religiously, which was 15 minutes everyday, it could be any time of the day. These couple of days the pain reduced to a manageable level, and I could actually move my head from side to side without much problem. Even my friends could tell the difference. I understand neck pain has different causes and intensity, it also depends on how you take care of yourself, what kind of bed/pillow you use, etc. This product may not be for everyone, but it helps me and I'd like to share my experience here for everyone's reference.

title: LOVE!

title: Lightweight and runs large - REVIEW UPDATED
text:
UPDATE: I wore this belt for 3 weeks to support a broken rib. I was on a vacation with long airplane flights, carried backpacks, and walked miles daily. The belt helped to support my rib and back. I had to wrap the belt tight occasionally and that necessitated the Velcro being attached directly to the belt fabric, not the other Velcro tab. I was worried that this would shred the fabric but it did not! it was nice to be able to adjust the tightness of the belt easily. I was hesitant to buy this because of the negative reviews but it has been a great little rib belt. And it is still elastic and in great shape to use again (I hope not though!). I updated my stars from 3 to 4. It is a very comfortable belt.

I've worn the rib belt for two days now with no tearing or shredding as reported by other users. However, the big flaw is that there are velcro tabs on either end that should match up to secure the belt. Unless you are the exact size of the belt, the female velcro is useless. I have to wrap the belt halfway again around my torso to get any kind of compression. The male velcro does attach to the belt material securely but I can see the lightweight material eventually shredding from adjusting and removing the belt on a daily basis. The belt material is lightweight and elasticity holds once you get the belt positioned.

It is comfortable to wear and it does help secure my broken rib while allowing me to breathe. it stays in place and doesn't roll. But if you need a heavier (tighter) compression, you might want to get something sturdier.

Overall, it is a comfortable belt to wear when you need light compression. It fits nicely under the girls so there is no pinching there either. I will use this until it wears out but I also ordered a heavier belt to wear (with two straps) when I am lifting or need a heavier compression factor.

title: Slow down the signs of aging by nourishing skin tissues
text:
I am not new to the use of essential and carrier oils, but using sea buckthorn oil was a new experience for me even though I had read about its use in nourishing the tissues in your skin and body and that it had a long history in regional folk medicines dating back thousands of years.

While I already have self made oil and lotion blends that I use for facial and body skin that I am very happy with, I am always open to learning new things and improving on what's there. So I was really curious and attracted to sea buckthorn due to its healing and rejuvenating effects on the skin and wanted to give it a try. I saw this product on Amazon and since US Organic Group wasn't a supplier that I was familiar with I had to research first before I was willing to purchase something that I was planning to use on my skin. I realize that reviews are not meant to be about manufacturer, but the manufacturer plays a key role for me in something like essential oils. One thing that swayed me in giving this manufacturer a try is not only because the product certified organic, but also that their products are 100% cruelty free. If you do a little further searching you will find that this company seems to have wellness in their DNA with affiliations to some other interesting organizations.

The oil itself has what I would call a deep amber or red orange color and viscous. It has a bit of a musky scent to it, although you can't really smell unless you hold it up directly to your nose. It can stain your skin, especially if you fail to dilute sufficiently. However, this is temporary and washes off easily.

It's a great exfoliator, skin cleanser and good for healing the skin. There have actually been studies done which show that daily use helps slow down the signs of aging by nourishing skin tissues. What's there not to love about that!

My facial skin is extremely sensitive and I have gotten to the point that I will know almost immediately if my skin likes what I am putting on it or not. I know some people may think that I am a little nuts, but it's true in my case. The reason I bring this up, is that when I used this product in my blend and apply it to my face, I can feel my skin reacting positively.

This is a very concentrated oil, and I recommend that you use sparingly. Also make sure that you dilute with a good carrier oil. There are a number of other essential oils that are good for your skin which you can add in your blend such as carrot seed, rose hip, lavender, frankincense, geranium and others. I can't tell you what blend works best in your particular case as everyone is unique. There are a lot of good articles that will help you get started. Whatever blend/s you come up with, I do recommend you include sea buckthorn given its ability to promote skin hydration, regeneration and elasticity, and even helps treat acne.

title: This device appears to produce excessive EMFs (electromagnetic fields)
text:
My entire family has had 1-2 Dohm machines in their bedroom for years now. And recently, I started researching EMF's (electromagnetic fields) and a concept known as 'dirty electricity'. My interest was peaked because the new home we moved into has solar panels and 2 different Smart Meters. Both are known for their EMF and dirty electricity production, so I was concerned our exposure may have increased.

I ordered a $40 EMF reader from Amazon, and began checking the EMF levels in and around our home. Quite by accident, I discovered that the Dohm produces far more EMF's than anything else in or around our home. To put things in perspective, the Smart Meters generated up to 250uTs, and our running microwave produced anywhere from 50 to 80uTs. The Dohm completely maxed out my reader! I believe it goes to 300uTs, so obviously the Dohm produces more than that.

And even more disturbing is that it STAYED maxed out. On the Smart Meters, the value would spike in the 200's, but then drop down and jump all over the place. But not the Dohm, it pegged the reader right away and stayed there. Even on the low setting! I realize there are differing opinions regarding the safe levels of EMF's, but this seems way too high. Especially for something that you are likely sleeping next to, for many hours at a time.

I have retired all of our Dohm machines, and will not be using them again.

title: Once hated, now prized.
text:
When I first heard one of these I HATED it. I was in an office out somewhere and it was already quiet in the room. All I could hear was this loud constant whoosh and it rivaled the noise in my head. I could not stand it.

But my husband started running a box fan in the bedroom at night and I was getting cold. Not to mention dust I'm allergic to would fly if it'd been a few days after vacuuming. I thought of this unit. I was already used to the fan noise at night. This thing had to improve the shiver/dust situation.

Oh, did it. It's become essential for my husband to get good sleep at night, and I've noticed when it's off that I go to sleep better and faster once I turn it on, especially now that I'm not freezing from all that blowing box fan air.

Months later I realized I was constantly agitated from high noise levels in a poorly sound-proofed home, but didn't know how to fix it. In the meantime, I'd bought a unit for my dad because trains were waking him up at night. However, it annoyed him like it had first annoyed me, so he didn't continue to use it. Then I thought of this unit and wondered if it might actually help mask the daytime noises, so Dad let me bring it home.

I regret not getting one sooner.

In a noisy environment, this thing gives me peace of mind. In my home office I can finally think when my husband is watching the yapper (TV) in the other room. And the kids and dogs amping up the noise, along with my constant companion, Tinnitus, fade away in this sweet, soothing whoosh.

My tinnitus makes me sensitive to high pitched noises, so I'm grateful I can adjust the pitch to what feels best to my ears. Perhaps that's why the first unit I heard drove me nuts--wrong pitch for me. I close most of the top and side holes for a lower pitch. Open them for a higher, louder pitch, and I start climbing the walls, but others might like it much better than what feels good to my being.

This was by far a valuable purchase for us and I recommend it to anyone needing some mental solitude in a loud environment.

title: Single Speed is HIGH SPEED
text:
I'd like to thank a previous reviewer who confirmed, before I ordered, that this SS single speed gives you the high speed (Loudest) setting.

Yes: this SS unit sounds just like the LOUDEST setting on the Dual Speed unit.

I had a DS unit on High right next to this SS unit and they sound the same. Very happy. I'll probably be ordering a third one for the other end of the house. I have a DS for my bedroom (I like the low setting if I have a migraine) but I use this SS in a Computer/TV room with a window overlooking my neighbor's barking dogs.

If you have a noisy neighborhood, or just want white-noise to fall asleep by I highly recommend this product. During the first week it actually kept me awake-but since then I find it indispensable. I use them during the day to drown out barking dogs and street noise while I read or watch TV.

These devices do very well against: dogs, kids playing, cars driving by and other noises. They do NOT drown out lawnmowers, snowblowers or booming car stereos as well. I found that out when my neighbor's lawn/snow removal service started showing up after midnight on occasion. I will say that while I can still here those things while reading--if I was asleep I don't think those things would wake me up. I LOVE THIS THING!!!!!!!!

title: Great sound muffling device!
text:
I am a Massage Therapist and I like this device for two reasons:
1) I place it just outside my treatment room door and turn it up all the way. I have tested it by having someone speak really loud in my office and now you cannot hear the exact words said and it covers up almost all sounds if the conversation is done at normal voice levels...so it helps keep client confidentiality.
2) It muffles the sounds coming into my office space from the hallway when people are walking, talking or being loud near my office.
Combined with playing soft music in my space, this is a great combination for my needs.

title: I bought one, loved it, bought another; Update: got one for baby, too!
text:
I bought the first one for my wife-to-be because she said she was having trouble sleeping and the fan helped. Bingo! This simple device is in constant use and I, too, like the effect.

My mother has had trouble sleeping for years. She would use the TV to put her to sleep (which I could never understand). She was up at all hours and she never got a good night's sleep. So I bought the second one and had it shipped to her. Bingo! She's now sleeping better than ever. In fact, she recently told me that she forgot to turn it on the other night and still slept well. (I have to believe that's because she is sleeping regularly now.)

If you have trouble sleeping for whatever reason, this seems to do the trick. $40 is a small price to pay for a consistent and good night's sleep.

Hint: since the device should be across the room, I also got an extension cord that has a switch that extends off of it (it's like a T configuration) so my wife can turn it on and off from the bedside.

Update: we just had our first baby four months ago. I immediately got another one for the baby's room. Seems to help her fall and stay asleep. (She's been a good sleeper from the beginning, though, so I can't say it is some miracle cure for babies that don't sleep well.)

title: This is the second unit I've purchased in the last ...

title: helps with noisy neighbors
text:
Living in a downstairs apartment + having sensitive ears = torture. After months of ear plugs and my upstairs neighbors loud stomping still distracting me from studying, I finally caved in and splurged on this sound conditioner. I was looking for a white noise machine that would block out the loud behemoth and obnoxious stomping upstairs. Neighbors, am I right -__-? The kid upstairs LOVES to skip, by the way. But enough about my neighbor troubles!!!

This machine has definitely helped. If it were a little less pricey, say around $30 or $40 , it would get more stars, but at $60 it's just okay. At first the noise was distracting, but with the machine on I was able to concentrate despite the loud click clack of hooves upstairs.

I'm a student and am permanently hibernating at home with my mountain of homework =], and this machine helps keep my attention on my studies. If you're an insomniac, this machine might also help, because even though I've had trouble sleeping, this machine makes me sleepy within ten minutes.

So the sound conditioner would have five stars if it were less pricey, but I'd say that it is *still* worth its price.

title: Love the product in general; my unit has developed a rattle
text:

I purchased an additional MARPAC unit for myself a couple of years ago to take on business travel, and it has developed a very annoying irregular rattle that conflicts with the white noise. The rattle becomes somewhat less pronounced if I place the unit on an angle, rather than flat on its base, so I try to find something in each hotel room to prop it up with. I am not sure whether if the inner workings are less durable than they were in the earlier models, or if I just had bad luck with this unit. I am outside the warranty period, so this is a disappointment.

title: Works exactly as expected
text:
I really like this as I like to do a Epsom salt and or baking soda food soak now and again and I just wanted something simple with a handle and had hoped for something taller so that I could have water up around my ankles. This is perfect! Very easy to use, large enough for my odd wide in the toe feet. I haven't had my husband see if his feet would fit length wise yet, but I think they would, this is fairly good sized.

I was especially pleased with the way it pours. When done you can pour the water easily out of the heel side as there is a bit of a notch in the toe side in the lip of the "bucket" to tip and pour everything out, then rinse and slosh with some soapy water and rinse out clean and let it air dry before the next use. After a few uses I will clean it a little more thoroughly with a rag or possibly even see how it fairs in the dishwasher. Anyway, when you pour the water out nothing dribbles down the sides or anything, the foot/bottom of the bucket stays dry unless you've gotten it wet or set it in a puddle yourself.

The only thing that I wish was different was the ridge down the middle of the bottom. I am guessing this is more so built in support to make the bucket more sturdy, but it forces you to keep your feet straight forward, whereas I would much rather be able to move them around more, but like I said, that is very minor. Oh, and there's also little arch support bumps along the middle, not a high enough arch support for my feet, but probably would be for most. Also, large bumps, kind of like pebbles on the bottom, I imagine this is to keep your feet elevated so that the soak will get to the bottoms of your feet. Unless you are standing in the "bucket" they are very comfortable.

title: Wonderfully-Soothing Baby Oil with Coconut Oil
text:
I do not have a baby on which to use this baby oil. I wanted to try it as a moisturizer for myself. I value coconut oil and use it daily, due to its wonderful health properties. Consequently, I was eager to try this mixture of baby oil and coconut oil. The first thing I noticed is its fresh and gentle scent of baby oil combined with coconut oil. It is a wonderful, light scent. I regularly use baby oil as a moisturizer, and I noticed that this oil is a little thicker than traditional baby oil, and, although it does absorb well into the skin, it does not absorb as quickly. For these reasons, I believe that this would be a better massaging oil than the traditional baby oil or baby lotion. As a moisturizer for adults, I believe it might be better used at night, as it doesn't absorb immediately into the skin. It did make my skin feel soft and smooth and soothed, leaving behind a light, fresh scent. It is ultra-gentle and great for sensitive skin. It contains no parabens, phthalates, dyes, mineral oil, formaldehyde, or harsh fragrances. This product is not tested on animals. The pump bottle is great for dispensing this oil in small amounts.

I was given a free sample of this product in exchange for an unbiased review.

title: Use this oil to relax your little one and get them ready for a soothing sleep
text:
Petite Planet Soothing Massage Oil is enriched with coconut oil created especially to nourish your little one's dry or sensitive skin.

This oil is infused with coconut oil and is perfect to use after bath time.

Years ago when my son was an infant, we would massage him with lotion before bedtime every night. He was my best sleeper. I now read that this practice has been routine in South Asia for centuries to support relaxation, bonding, and happy development. They often used coconut oil for its ability to soothe a baby's delicate skin.

I am now a grandmother and encourage my children to continue this practice. This oil is hypoallergenic and dermatologist-tested. It is also free of parabens, phthalates, dyes, mineral oil, formaldehyde, or harsh fragrances.

title: Great
text: I find it so weird that something made with coconut oil stays liquid at room temperature and comes out of a lotion bottle without gumming up the bottle. But it does indeed work. And it has a light, baby pleasant smell. Adults might not prefer this for themselves, just because the scent is a bit newborn. It works nicely, moisturizes well, and is perfect for massages. Five stars.

title: Babies or Pensioners
text:
I cannot say how much I love this stuff!! I was becoming a self-scratching post with this long, dry winter tormenting me. I squirted some on my legs to relieve the worst itch I've ever had from dry weather--it worked immediately. It deadened the itch, began to soothe my skin, and hydrated like a dream. The scent was awesome, too. I felt like I was at the beach--Hawaiin Tropic comes to mind.

title: Weird synthetic smell
text:
I thought that a baby oil with coconut oil would smell a little like coconut. I was wrong-Petite Planet Soothing Baby Oil with Coconut smells nothing like coconut. It has a weird, synthetic "fresh" smell that I do not care for at all. I do like it better than the "baby fresh" scent products had when my kids were little.

Fragrance aside, this oil absorbs well, and quickly, leaving skin soft and not greasy. It does not seem to stain clothes, but I have not really checked, or use this before putting on clothes that I care about. The kids I work with find the scent weird, and one of them asked me if I had used the lotion they have at the hospital. It gives my skin some much needed moisture, but it does not take long before my skin needs another application.

text: This is a nice baby oil product. The main oil is soy which I feel they should be a bit more up front about as soy allergies are fairly common, but it is listed in the ingredients with the second being the coconut. Thankfully no one in the house has soy allergies, and as for the formula it is gentle on the skin and did not cause irritation to even on sensitive areas. The fragrance is pleasant and tropical but a bit too strong. It does work well for massage, not drying too quickly or leaving the skin too wet. It leaves the skin hydrated, and as it is for massage the absorption is slow so I find a gentle blotting after helps. Overall it is a nice oil, it is good on sensitive skin and has a tropical fragrance.

This basket is made by the same company and the description says that it fits the steering column of the KneeRover Go, however the mounting bracket doesn't hold it on securely. My fiance had to really work on making it somewhat secure, but it still loosens and slides down. It seems that the bracket was made for a thicker steering column. He's going to have to do some additional work on it to get it to stay in place.

The basket itself is useful - much better than not having one. However, if you are going to advertise it as being made to work with a specific model of your KneeRover scooters, the mounting bracket should be made to fit securely on that model. Your customers should not have to do extra work to make the hardware securely attach so the basket doesn't slide down.

text:

At first, I was uncertain about its "anti-reflux" valve and its drain closure but I'm happy to say that so far it has worked perfectly. It may cost as much as several of the common bedside urinals but probably won't need to be emptied till morning. Calibrated markings also estimate volume which can be helpful if monitoring kidney output. Better sleep worth the extra $$ to me.
UPDATE:. I would add another star if possible. A few days ago, I felt that I was having a problem with the drain clamp on the system. I emailed a note to the vendor asking if I could buy these separate. I quickly received an email saying they would take care of it. To my surprise, I received a USPS priority mail package in two days with a complete new system!!
I've sometimes lamented that online commerce sorely lacks the customer service we used to know with local shops. This vendor is doing his best to change that perception. I highly recommend the vendor and the product.

text: I bought this spray for the extended hose and the type of diverter. Very easy to install. I didn't like the idea of drilling holes so I hung it on the shower caddy. My complaint is the diverter started to leak and not at the connections where I can fix the problem. The leak is a smooth cut (like an exacto blade) in the center of valve. I didn't have to use tools to install so there are no scratches or damage to the valve. I am in a loose loose situation, There are no options to contact the manufacturer, Amazon will not allow a return or replacement. I can use putty or tape but that will look tacky, and may not work, or head out to Home depot to search for a compatible diverter valve. Although I like the features this  hose spray is not worth it.

title: Great product !
text:
First of all, I'd like to say that ALL the bad or less than great reviews by some purchasers, are without fundament. This is a really good product and, you can't beat the price ! On top of that the seller : Drive Medical (thru Amazon) delivered the product inside of 3 days
As soon as it came, I put the hose inside of a 3/4" PVC pipe and left it to relax overnight to get the coil shape out of it.
The diverter valve is sturdy plastic and, well made (mine came a little hard to operate but, with a little silicone spray and gentle twisting back and forth, it finally operated freely and smoothly.
Now for the installation: You have to use your imagination and think that you just can't dry-screw the fittings the way they came : You HAVE to use Teflon tape on the male parts of ALL the fittings including the hand held shower attachment(otherwise they all are going to leak!). Don't forget to use the three washers that came with it.Just remember that all the fittings for this product are plastic and cannot be overtightened with a wrench !!.

The only part I do not like is the holder because the shower attachment keeps slipping off; if you'd rather not drill holes in the wall use silicone to hold it. The dog is going to love this thing and ,so will my back. Would highly recommend it, don't let the nay-sayers and "un-handy" installers sway you. I took a chance because the price will mislead you into thinking it's a cheap product but, I was pleasantly proven wrong.

title: Good Monitor
text:
The pads work as expected.

Kerr Medical shipped fully assembled. All I had to do was add three C batteries to the alarm and program the alarm to recognize the pads.

Programming was just pressing a pin into the back of the alarm until two LED lights lit up in the alarm, then sit on - and get off of the pads, then press the pin into the back one time to finish.

The plastic pads make a little stiff plastic "crinkle" noise if they are not under a mattress or couch cushion. This draws attention of my senior Mom and can lead to repetitive questions, or removal if I'm not watching.

The alarm is made for wall mounting or setting on something. My preference is slipping it into a front pants pocket. The alarm is larger and heavier than a wallet but it works ok for me and I wear loose fit jeans. If it goes off, I just reach into the pocket and reset the chime.

When Mom is on the couch I may be at the computer in front of her on the floor. When the couch (chair pad) alarm goes off, she is typically already on her feet and stepping away.

Left on her own she would go onto the porch in summer heat, so this is just adequate warning. With her fall risk I don't know if another product would alert me faster or physically impede her (which I really don't want to do).

The directions (mention) imply that this also works with "Cordless Floor Mat", "Cordless Nurse" call button and "Cordless motion sensor".

The "Low volume" is not disruptive, about as loud as a typical cell phone ring.

This may be like the [[ASIN:B0043RFKME Bed Alarm and Bed Pad (Cord Free)]] if it uses the 433-EC alarm, but this includes a chair pad (see their reviews for more feedback). One of those reviews mentions a power plug adapter - but I did not receive one for this product.

title: Wish they would improve it because it's a nice little table for the bed.
text: I've had this table a couple of years. Cons: It has a permanent "lean downward" towards the center of the bed. Also, one of the legs kept sliding down (the button kept slipping instead of staying in the hole) causing that side of the table to cave, and everything would fall off. My husband drilled a hole and screwed that leg permanently at the level of the other leg. IF the manufacturer wanted to improve on the design, they could insert corner supports under the table top where it meets the legs. That could prevent the "sag" or lean downwards towards the center of the bed. The other way it could be permanently improved would be to create the table-to-leg at about a 50 to 55 degree setting instead of the 45 degree (which causes the sag). Even placing diagonal metal supports from the legs to the table would keep the table up and horizontal to the bed. Pros: It's very easy to slide out and replace when you need to change sheets. The table top also has a "lip" all the way around that helps keep items from sliding off the table. It's lightweight, easy to clean, doesn't rust (we live on an island) and you can place it closer to you or farther down the bed, wherever you want it without any trouble at all. If you do spill anything (remember the lean?) you have more time to mop it up because of the lip around the top.

title: This is 2nd one of these I bought. The exact same bag cost me $40 more from a medical supply store in Manhattan
text: I first got this exact same model number EZ Access Walker Bag in January when I went to a medical supply store in Manhattan located near my doctor's office to buy an immediately needed walker. The bag cost me $59.95. It turned out to be much more useful than I thought it would be, particularly at my job. With the bag on the side of the walker, and with the zipper on the large pocket open, I am able to put a ream of paper in the bag to carry it  to our copier. I am able to put a gallon size bottle of water in the same large pocket to carry it from the refrigerator to my office. Tonight we had a lecture presentation and I was able to fill the large pockets (having bought a 2nd bag thru Amazon.com which arrived yesterday) with spoons, a container of milk, a bottle of Coffee Mate, Sugar, foam cups, all to bring to the refreshment table in the room for the presentation. It feels good to be able to do these relatively simple chores again, and not depend upon others to do them,  as I have had to do since 9 months ago when i first came down with a series of physical injuries which coincidentally led to a relapse of a plasma cell cancer which had been in remission for 14 years. I do only use the pockets for carrying items at work and at home. I use the walker outdoors only to walk from my house or from my office, or from one of my many medical appointments, to a waiting car service. The bag's zippered pocket stays closed and flat while outside, keeping the bag nice and flat and unobtrusive, as I feel I must be while outdoors. At 4'6", having lost over 5 inches in the past decade due to my illness, it had become very hard walking around the city's sidewalks filled with people so much taller, who it seemed were always walking into me, having not noticed me down there while talking on their cellphone. At home I add a removable tray to the walker, and now with two pockets, it has become so easy to transport things all over my house. So, I really love this walker bag for helping me feel so much less helpless than I did 2 months ago. And, as I stated up above, the 2nd bag that I bought thru amazon.com was 19.99, whereas the 1st bag cost me $59.95, which is a whopping $40 more, from a medical supply store in Manhattan. Oh, and I should mention how much less I saw the exact same Drive folding walker model on amazon.com selling for, than what I paid for it in the same medical supply store. Too upsetting, so I remind myself that I had no choice as I needed the walker immediately, and that was the price I paid for immediate.

title: A MIRACLE of RELIEF
text:
I found this to be an excellent product with a loud piercing sound that you could not sleep through. Since I was the only other person in the house, this was ideal when I was either in my own bedroom on the other side of the wall, or downstairs and in another room, or even yet another level further downstairs, in other words this was audible from level 1 to level 3. This alert *is* going to wake up anyone else in the house, in my opinion, unless their door is closed, they are a very heavy sleeper, their bedroom is far away, and maybe even then. Other reviewers have discussed how it is possible to muffle the sound by wrapping it in a towel or something, so it can be muted, but that was the last thing I was interested in.

The battery also lasts an extremely long time, something like a year or more of 24x7 use, and there is a highly visible blinking light to assure you the battery is still working (the light is small, and won't keep anyone awake).

This was some of the best money I've ever spent, allowing me to actually sleep in my own bed with absolute confidence I would be awakened no matter how deeply I was sleeping, and as exhausted as I was, I had begun to sleep very deeply without wanting to.

The instructions are very clear, just put the batteries in, adjust the mat under the sleeper, and hang the device on their doorknob or wherever - the cord beyween the mat and the alarm device was plenty long enough to be convenient. You can place the mat under the other person's shoulders, so that it goes off if their shoulders come off the mat (which is about a yard wide, so just rolling over on top of it will not trigger it), or you can place it under them lower down, around the middle of their ribs, so it is triggered only if they actually sit up. The device is sensitive and works immediately with no dangerous time lag, when pressure contact on the mat is removed. It does not go off if someone just rolls back and forth on it or shifts position. I experimented with the proper placement by lying on top of it myself, and adjusting its location to be under my ribs, so that it would go off when my shoulders got about 8" off the bed, as I was in the process of sitting up. It worked perfectly EVERY TIME.

I did not actually *use* the feature of the magnetic tether for detecting when someone sitting, gets up from a chair, but I did *test* it, and found it unobtrusive and lightweight to the sitting person, and extremely effective.

I said out loud to myself and to others, repeatedly, that this was the best money I'd ever spent in my life. I no longer had to sleep on the floor by the bed so I'd be physically stepped on and awakened, or on the floor in the hallway just outside the open door in the hopes I would hear activity and wake up in time, and no longer did I have to attempt to stay awake all night at the foot of the bed, in an uncomfortable chair, in case something happened.

This product was a miracle of relief to me, I have absolutely NO complaints about it, and only the HIGHEST praise.

It's simple to use, it works brilliantly, there is a reassuring light visible from at least 60 feet away (probably farther) so you know it's on, the light lets you know when the battery finally *does* begin to get weak, but the sound is still very loud and the device still works strongly for WEEKS after the "weak battery" light alert comes on, so there is NO concern about being surprised by it suddenly stopping working. title: Huge improvement on average walker wheels
text:
I bought these "off-road" walker wheels for a relative who is recovering from a mild stroke. He is at the point where he is supposed to be walking more and more each day. He has been cleared to do some of that walking outside in the driveway and even in the yard. It turns out that the thin 5" gray walker wheels that come on a standard walker don't work so well outside. I haven't had to use a walker before, but I gave it a shot and could feel how much the wheels bounced when they hit a little piece of gravel or a seam in the sidewalk. The grass? Disaster. The wheels sort of sunk into the damp ground and then I was stuck.

New wheels were a must.

I ended with these wheels from North American Health and Wellness. Unlike a lot of the walker wheels sold as "off-road," this pair had tread and was wider than normal wheels. Both of these factors are needed to make a significant difference in how the walker will handle rough spots in the road.

These wheels do come on standard 1" wide walker wheel attachment tubes. The axels on these wheels are higher than the regular wheels, so the setting for the tubes will lower than usual by 3 clicks. My relative usually has the wheels at a 7; for these, a 4. *** I don't think these wheels will work for a person whose walker wheel tubes are typically set at lower than a 4. *** They go on just like regular wheels. To make it easier to go through doorways, you may want to turn the wheels towards the inside of the walker.

The package also includes 2 of the biggest walker skis I have ever seen. We have not installed these yet as the physical therapist recommends staying with the caps on the back of the walker for a while. The skis are made of a thick, smooth resin and look like they will work well.

My relative has absolutely loved these wheels and finds them to be a ginormous improvement upon the old wheels. We don't think the tread makes that much difference as it is a fairly wide and shallow pattern that wouldn't get much traction. But the width of the wheels just gives him more stability, inside the house and out. Gravel on the sidewalk is not a problem anymore, and neither is grass. He also finds it easier to _stop_ on the wood floors inside the house, which I was unaware of being an issue. The material of the tires has slightly more give than the hard gray tires he had before; it must be just enough to respond to the exertion of pressure. However the tires work, he feels more stable and is happier about doing the physical therapy.

Do I recommend these wheels? Yes, if your doctor or physical therapist also recommends them. =-) I am not a doctor or a physical therapist or anyone else that knows how a change like larger tires on a walker could impact your or a loved one's physiology. Because I have not seen tires like this at any home medical supply company, what I would recommend if you want to try them is to just buy them and take them with you to your or your loved one's medical appointment. It will be easier for your medical professional to assess impact if they can see the wheels you're talking about and compare them to what you have now. And if they don't work out, you can return the unused wheels. There are other options that might work better for you or your loved one. The first bar, I had to peel off the wrapper because they bars had a coating of sticky caramel on half of the outside. Tasted fine but impossible to eat without making a total sticky mess.
Stuck them in the fridge for 15 minutes thinking it'd cool the caramel a bit but when I took them out the second one was pale looking color that didn't go away even after it got to room temp which was super weird, didn't look very appetizing either but still tasted fine. The rest never got their normal chocolate color back either, my guess is that they melted and cooling them messed em all up.
Overall, they were pretty tasty at least. I was glad that this bar's chocolate coating tasted a little better than ONE's kinda weird off-chocolate taste. title: That is why Glucosamine HCl is not sold by itself but with other ingredients that provide the sulphur like Chondroitin Sulfate
text:
Why did I select this product?

Glucosamine Sulfate is known to helps cartilage regeneration. Many supplements sold are Glucosamine HCl (hydrochloride) rather than Glucosamine Sulphate. Sulfate is needed to produce cartilage. That is why Glucosamine HCl is not sold by itself but with other ingredients that provide the sulphur like Chondroitin Sulfate. But many physicians consider that Chondroitin takes away the efficacy of the Glucosamine.

A study by ConsumerLab.com showed that many of the glucosamine/ chondroitin supplements do not contain the labeled amounts of ingredients. Also if some pills do not dissolve sufficiently, their ingredients might not be fully available for absorption in the body.

That is why I selected this product in powder and from a company that I begin to trust.

title: Very happy to have found this product, great job Julian Bakeries!
text:
***2017 Update***

After looking at a lot of protein powders from various different sources, eggs, meat, vegetables, milk, etc...I chose this one.

Below are the reasons:

-U.S. Based manufacturing and ingredient source, some powders are produced outside the U.S. and I have read there is metal or other contamination that can occur. Though I did not confirm this I assume U.S. based products would not have this issue or are safer than non-U.S. products.
-No filler ingredients, this is literally powder egg whites, which by default are a whole/natural protein source. Other powders have so much weird un-pronouncable "stuff" in them that you don't even know what your taking or how accurate the claims are.
-Non-GMO and no antibiotics used on chickens
-Eggs are cooked and not air dried (this prevents a avidin health issue), they are also pasteurized. This was confirmed by calling Julian Bakery's in California and an email to their nutritionist.
-No Soy, no Lactose! Large amounts of soy diets can cause hormonal issues for both men and women. Avoid soy proteins! I am also lactose intolerant so pure egg protein is great.
-Price per. protein comes to 30 g per. dollar., really good rate compared to other products out there.
-Low calories, basically you are taking in calories only for the protein not other fillers (e.g., sugars), it is about 4.32 calories per. protein
-The expiration dates are very reasonable, my two bags are about 2 year + to expiration.

-One con is that it does have a lot of salt (381 mg per serving), so if you are sensitive to it, or this is something you watch, it is something to keep in mind

One thing that stuck out is that the empty scoop weighs 9 grams and filled it is 34 grams, I am not sure why this is, maybe they are rounding the servings to a nice number. Technically each scoop has 25 grams (34 grams minus 9 grams) of powder, which i hopefully means it is 25 g of protein and additional 5 grams is just rounding since serving size is 30 grams.

***CORRECTION*** I realized that the scoop measures close to 30 grams, but its impossible to design something to pick up the exact amount of powder every single time, you will need a scale if you want exactly 30 grams every time, or just live with the fact you will scoop anywhere from 25-30 grams.

Overall good product and one of the best I found. The taste is so-so, that means it won't make you puke, but it isn't like ice-cream. It's just plain. I am in the middle of my first bag. Before protein powders became a fad and different brands/recipes went out on the market, in the 90's eggs were considered to be the best source of pure complete protein (i believe it still is). I am comfortable with putting this in my body over a long period of time on a daily basis due to its very very short ingredient list.

Please always consult a doctor before changing your diet or exercise program. I am not a doctor and nothing here is offered as health advice. Please as always verify everything once you receive the product or before you buy.

"Horsetail supplements should not be used for prolonged periods. text:
This is a very good and high quality product however...bone broth can affect the nervous system and it may be a good idea to do some research before adding it to your diet. I was very irritable during the time I was taking the product and now I know why - I have found out that the result of the long cook times for the bone broth supplements is a tremendous amount of glutamic acid. Glutamic acid and glutamate are highly regulated by the human brain. High amounts of glutamic acid can trigger seizures if you’re prone to them. It can also trigger other neurological symptoms you may already be sensitive to, including brain fog, migraine headaches, dramatic mood swings, stimming, and nervous tics.
I personally feel that there should be a warning on this type of products about possible side effects. People with MS should definitely not take it.

title: Product is mislabeled with incorrect serving size -- only provides 24 servings, not 34!
text:
UPDATE!!! (4/5/22)

Okay... I can't believe they actually did this. This seller is sleazy.

Instead of simply increasing the amount of blueberry powder you get -- which would have been the normal and decent thing to do IMO -- or decreasing the number of servings listed on the package (to make it accurate to what you're getting), they instead opted (after I complained in my review below, apparently) to REDUCE the total amount of blueberry powder you get (from 3.5g down to 2.5g) AND cut in HALF the recommended serving size from 2tsp. down to 1tsp., and are now claiming that by reducing the volume of actual blueberry powder you're getting by almost a third, they are MAGICALLY increasing the number of "apparent" servings you are getting by almost 30%, which is now claimed to be 48 servings versus the original 34 claimed servings (which was actually 24 servings). So, basically, by cutting the serving size in half, and reducing the powder weight by 29%, you're now getting 2x the actual previous number of servings (see my original review below).

I cannot believe people are this unethical in business on Amazon! Amazon needs to hold sellers like this accountable for their misleading advertising. Stop playing games and just deliver a good product at a fair and *straightforward* price and quit playing games with your amounts, serving sizes, and number of servings. It's very misleading -- and I believe this has been done very much intentionally.

/rant

------------------

Original review:

The packaging claims there are 34 servings. One serving is shown as being 2 tsp.

It was running out very fast, so I decided to measure how much a serving size weighed.

1 tsp weighs approximately 3.5 grams (averaged across a couple of teaspoons), thus a 2 tsp serving is 7 grams.

There are 6 ounces (allegedly -- I should have weighed it when I received the bag). Thus, the bag provides only 24 servings, not 34. Big difference! So, I was not imagining things. It really did run out fast (30% faster than it should have).

It is mislabeled as providing more servings than it actually does.

I'm annoyed because A) It's expensive, B) It ran out long before all the other smoothie ingredients I bought, which *will* last at least a month, as I expected this to do.

I wish I could get a refund. Not happy when products are mislabeled like this. I don't know if it's careless or deliberate to make it seem like you're getting more servings than you actually are in order to try to compete better with other products, as no, I would *not* have spent that much money for only 24 servings.

title: Fantastic Product
text:
I have been fermenting my own vegetables for some time now. I have tried various methods and recipes. I would not consider making fermented vegetables without this product.

I use 1 tablespoon of Himalayan Pink Salt per head of cabbage, 1 packet of Body Ecology Vegetable Starter, 1 rounded teaspoon of organic honey (locally purchased from our bee-keeper). I put these ingredients into my Vita Mix with some of the vegetables and I pulverize it using pure Alkaline water. I then put the brine on the shredded vegetables and stir well. I add additional water if needed. I use different amounts of salt but not on the other ingredients. Just one packet of starter, etc. is enough.

I then pack the vegetables into a German crock (purchased here on Amazon) and I pack them down using a potato masher. When the pot is packed, I add whole cabbage leaves to place on top to keep small pieces of vegetables from floating. I add the stones that came with the Crock on top of the leaves. I push them down with the potato masher and make sure that the water rises above the stones.

I then leave this for 7 days at room temperature. When fermented, I place the vegetables in mason jars and store in my refrigerator. I eat these vegetables daily. I like them with scrambled eggs for breakfast or a nice piece of meat for dinner as a side dish.

I am always making fermented vegetables. My favorite is organic green cabbage and carrots. But you can use almost any vegetable and add red pepper and garlic if desired. The choice is yours. My crock pot is always in use.

I have read the Body Ecology book which I would also recommend to anyone interested in the health benefits from fermented foods.

I have tried other starters, but I like Body Ecology Culture Starter the very best. By using a starter, I KNOW that the friendly bacteria is in my vegetables. This culture contains lactococcus species, leuconostoc species and lactobacillus species. You get a lot of the right type of friendly bacteria for your colon, immune system and general health.

I haven't used this starter, so my non-recommendation isn't really about the starter itself if purchased elsewhere. I'm not sure what the starter should smell like or be like, so this may or may not be a fair rating; this was my first time ordering anything like this. My review is mostly about the starter being offered by the current seller (aliga online).

First, the box was inserted in a very small offering of bubble wrap (the top of the box had no wrapping, though), inside of a non-padded shipping envelope. So no real protection there and the box was a bit smooshed, but it's not breakable so I guess that's okay. However, when I opened the envelope I was immediately overwhelmed by patchouli. I have no idea if culture starters are supposed to naturally smell like patchouli, but I wouldn't think so. It was so bad that it gagged me, though I'm sure that reflex won't happen to those who enjoy that scent (I really dislike it). I did take the box out of the envelope and slide off the bubble wrap to take some pictures, but I knew I wouldn't be able to keep it and use it with such a strong scent. No way. Lol.

The culture did ship quickly and the seller was congenial and emailed me a shipping label to print out for return. I had some issues with the download and they sent me a couple different files for me to try, so I appreciate their patience with that. However, it took 3 weeks for a refund after I sent back the package. After waiting almost 2 weeks with no word from them or Amazon, I emailed to ask how and when I should expect my refund. They replied that they mailed it out and should expect it the next week on a certain day.

That day came and went and I checked the tracking number they'd given me, only to find that it was not even sent out yet. The number they'd given me was something like a parking place for a package (not sure how to describe it). Essentially, they reserved the tracking number but it didn't mean the package had been sent. So I emailed them again and asked what was going on and they said that it should be there in 2 days, which was a Friday. They said something about this electronic notice thing, saying that's why I couldn't track it, but in my experience when I go to track something, I can always see where it is in the country at any given time. For this package, it wasn't showing it to be anywhere at all. So anyways, Friday came and went, too, and the refund didn't show up until the next Tuesday.

I wasn't happy about that and how the refund was given, either. They sent a check to me written out to "Cash". I wasn't sure why they didn't write it out to me, or for that matter, why they didn't do the refund through Amazon like other sellers have done (well, I've only had to do this one other time with a vendor through Amazon). I guess because it's cheaper to write out a check than do a credit transaction? I really don't know. It seemed strange to me. I had to deposit the check into my own account because there isn't a bank here that the check was written from; I hope that it clears okay. If not, I'll be sure to update my review.

So even though they were cordial and speedy with their replies throughout our transaction and I eventually received a refund, I'm afraid I can't recommend buying a culture starter through this vendor. I think if you really want this starter, you should look into buying it directly from the manufacturer's website or maybe find one comparable at the Cultures for Health site. There are just some things you shouldn't buy from Amazon; culture starters and batteries to name a couple. Lol. Normally, I have very good experiences here, but not with those things.

Something that I've realized in the past week or so is that you don't really need an expensive starter if you just use a capsule or two of a high-quality probiotic supplement (one with at least a billion cells). It's a lot cheaper to go that route, anyways, and I hear it's just as acceptable for a starter. I remember hearing about this a long time ago, but didn't know of anyone really using this method until recently (from a reviewer of a fermenting book), so I just hadn't experimented with it at all (well, I wasn't really ready to start fermenting back then). Now that I know that this method does work--and works well--I won't be ordering another starter; I already had a starter here in my fridge and didn't realize it--lol.

I can recommend both Renew Life and Garden of Life probiotics because neither of them contain fillers, btw. You don't even need those, technically, since the food usually has sufficient bacteria on it to make it ferment, but using a starter or probiotics speeds things up and makes it so there usually isn't any mold growth on top of the jar that you need to clean each day, and you don't have to use as much (if any) salt. Using organic foods is best since they have more biological activity on them due to not being sprayed with pesticides. From what I understand, the proper way to use the probiotic as starter is to mix it into a small amount of water and add to the jar, then top it off with purified water or brine, if needed. If you do a web search on "Vikraut and Vikimchi", you will find a site that has instructions for using probiotics in kimchi and sauerkraut; they don't use salt in the recipes. You could add salt, if you wish, but I'm not sure how much could be tolerated by the probiotic cells. I don't think it would hurt to add enough to taste.

title: If you want to know about Magnesium......
text:
As many now know, magnesium is need for hundreds of chemical processes in the human body. Most people buy it for muscle relaxation, sleep or to relieve muscle cramps at night, but there many other positives to taking magnesium. Almost everyone is low in Mg, unless they supplement. But here's the KEY, all Mg is not created equal.
The lowest quality, least soluble form is Magnesium Oxide. This is basically useless and is actually the "rust" or oxidated form of magnesium. This is also the cheapest and most magnesium supplements use only this form.
The next up the chain, with a little better absorption and a little more expensive is Magnesium Citrate.
The magnesium forms that are considered top tier, with best absorption is a class called chelated Magnesium. They included Magnesium Malate, Mg Theonate, Mg glycinate and bisglycinate and a few others. These are the forms that are the most soluble and the best quality......BUT they also cost the most.
This Magnesium uses a chelated form, which is one of the best. "Bisglycinate Chelate" is the form used in this supplement.
This supplement uses a superior form of magnesium, is more absorbable and more bioavailable. I personally take this and also recommend this to my patients.
Side note:. Too much magnesium, taken too frequently, will cause diarrhea, but you can work up the dose slowly to avoid this.

text:
I got this as a breastfeeding supplement, since the reason barley and oats are supposed to help is because they contain beta glucan, especially barley. I found it here in a concentrated form while looking for different ingredients to make lactation cookies. Buying this was ultimately easier and cheaper than buying the ingredients for lactation snacks.
This supplement, along with pumping a little extra here and there, more than doubled my milk supply. I went from barely pumping enough to feed my baby to pumping 16-20 ounces extra daily after about 10-14 days. Also, the milk I made began to look different, the fat rose to the surface when stored in the fridge but the color of the milk stayed the same, whereas now that I have not used this supplement for a week to see what would happen, my milk looks much clearer after the fat rises.
The reason I'm not giving this five stars is because of the texture. It wants to settle at the bottom of the glass, and it changes the consistency of everything. One person in the reviews mentioned putting it in their coffee- it sat at the bottom and made the consistency of the coffee itself very thick. I found it best in juice, after letting it sit for a minute it absorbed a lot of the juice and thickened to a smoothie texture. Would definitely be best in an actual smoothie, but as it stands I hate washing blenders.
Overall, it worked for what I wanted. Would recommend to mothers who want to boost the supply and quality of their milk.
